name: Swahili Call Center Audio Dataset (single channel)
notes: Vendor-scale 8 kHz call-centre audio claimed at 194k hrs split by locale (sw 77.8k, KE 111.2k, UG 5.3k) with PII muting; the hour claim is very large and unverified - treat with caution, but it is the only telephone-domain Swahili corpus at scale.

name: WorldSpeech (disco-eth)
notes: 24 kHz corpus mined from national parliaments, public broadcasters, public-domain audiobooks and international institutions, with CER/SNR/DNSMOS quality scores; Horn languages are tagged but hour shares are small.

name: Meta MMS-lab (Massively Multilingual Speech, labelled)
notes: Aligned single-speaker New Testament readings in 1,107 languages, 36.8k h train / 3.5k dev / 4.4k test. Africa is the largest single region: the released ASR model covers 363 African languages and 91% of them reach CER<=5%. The audio itself is NOT openly redistributed (third-party scripture copyright) - only the models are; practitioners must re-derive alignments from the source Bible audio.

name: Global Recordings Network (GRN) audio library
languages: Thousands of African languages and dialects
many African languages, creoles and pidgins
notes: Gospel-message and Bible-story audio in more than 6,000 languages and dialects - by far the widest language coverage of any African audio source, including many languages with no other recordings. Short programmes, variable recording quality, language labels only (no transcripts). This is exactly the corpus Meta crawled to build MMS-unlab (3,809 usable languages).
language_note: This source describes its coverage in prose rather than naming individual languages, so it carries no ISO 639-3 codes. The source's own wording is kept in `languages`.

name: African Next Voices programme (continental)
languages: 18 African languages (7 South African confirmed; Kenyan and Nigerian nodes additional)
notes: Gates-Foundation-backed 2025 programme building a multi-country African speech corpus, executed by country nodes (University of Pretoria DSFSI for South Africa; Digital Umuganda appears to run the Swahili/Kenya node - it publishes anv_test_data_nt_swahili). The 3,000 h / 7-language South African node is verified; the widely quoted 9,000 h / 18-language programme total could NOT be verified from a primary source in this pass - treat as unconfirmed.
language_note: This source describes its coverage in prose rather than naming individual languages, so it carries no ISO 639-3 codes. The source's own wording is kept in `languages`.

name: Mozilla Common Voice v26.0 (Scripted Speech) - African languages
notes: Largest single open multilingual African speech resource: ~85 African languages in v26.0. Verified per-language total hours: Kinyarwanda 2384, Swahili 1065, Kabyle 694, Luganda 561, Arabic 158, Dholuo 112, Kalenjin 88, Taita 56, Oromo 26, Dagbani 28, Igbo 19, Ibibio 18, Nigerian Pidgin 15, Baatonum 14, Baoule 14, Hausa 13, Aja 13, Yoruba 8, Amharic 3, Afrikaans 1.7, Tswana 4.9, Twi 1.4; plus a large 2024-26 Cameroon/Central-Africa expansion of ~45 languages at roughly 10-19 h each (Basaa, Duala, Ewondo, Ghomala, Medumba, Bafut, Kom, Bamun, Fe'fe', Bulu, Eton, Mundang, Tupuri, Mada, Kwasio, Tunen, Cameroon Pidgin, Chokwe, Luba-Kasai, Hemba, Nyungwe, Koti, Rombo, Tem, Nawdm, Gen, Fang, etc.). Validated hours are typically 60-90% of total; South African languages (Zulu, Xhosa, Venda, Tsonga, Ndebele, Sotho) are near-empty (<5 h).

name: UGSpeechData (GitHub distribution repo)
notes: Official HCI-Lab repo with AUDIO_ID.csv metadata and Dropbox download pointers for the 5,000-hour corpus.

name: UGSpeechData (University of Ghana HCI Lab, Lacuna Fund)
notes: 1,000 h of audio per language (5,000 h total) of which 100 h per language is transcribed; rich per-clip metadata (gender, age, device, environment, locale). By far the largest Ghanaian speech collection, but the ND clause blocks derivative distribution.

name: Afrivoice_Ethiopia (Digital Umuganda)
notes: 316,000+ clips, 213 GB, split into unscripted, scripted and 'expert' categories with contributor-disjoint train/val/test. Transforms the Ethiopian picture: previously Amharic had only ALFFA and ~3 h of Common Voice. Sidama and Wolaytta had essentially no prior open speech data.

name: Omnilingual ASR (paper and 1,600-language model release)
notes: Paper and facebookresearch/omnilingual-asr code; documents the per-language coverage list to check which Central African languages have transcribed data.

name: Afrivoice_Swahili (Digital Umuganda)
notes: Largest open transcribed corpus for any African language: 561,139 clips, ~249 GB, image-prompted speech across agriculture (744 h), health (618 h), finance (606 h), government (579 h) and education (550 h), locale sw_KE. CC-BY-4.0. Apparently the Swahili node of African Next Voices.

name: Afrivoice (Digital Umuganda, v1)
notes: Image-prompted triples (JPEG image + WAV description + transcript where available), ~1.21 TB. Per language: Shona 574 h (100 transcribed), Fulani 527 h (102), Wolof 531 h (103), Somali 536 h (105), Malagasy 516 h (102), Lingala 517 h (101). The transcribed slice is only ~100 h/language but the raw audio is enormous.

name: GRN African Speech (Global Recordings Network, packaged)
notes: 1,551 language/dialect subsets of 15s 16kHz voice-only clips filtered from GRN gospel recordings - the only broad source covering Liberian Pidgin English, Cabo Verde Criolo and regional English/French/Portuguese varieties. Audio remains (c) GRN, research use only.

name: ADI17 (Arabic Dialect Identification, 17 countries)
notes: ~3,033 h train + 57 h dev/test of YouTube audio labelled by country; distributed as YouTube URLs + timestamps because of copyright, so it needs scraping, but it is by far the largest pool of North African dialect audio and is widely repurposed for ASR pre-training.

name: AfriVoices-KE / African Next Voices - Kenya
notes: Largest Kenyan-language speech corpus to date: 669 hrs scripted + 2,336 hrs unscripted across 11 domains (40% agriculture/food), speaker-disjoint splits; Gates-funded African Next Voices programme.

name: Swivuriso: The South African Next Voices Multilingual Speech Dataset (ZA-African Next Voices)
notes: Largest SA speech dataset ever released: ~3,000 h (zul 503, xho 504, sot 504, tsn 502, tso 500, ven 251, nbl 252), scripted + unscripted, agriculture/health/general, 48 kHz. Gated: licence forbids TTS/voice cloning. Also on GitHub (dsfsi/za-african-next-voices) and Zenodo record 17776289.

name: WAXAL (Google Research release note)
notes: Official announcement with the collection methodology (image-prompted elicitation, 50+ topics) and the partner list including University of Ghana (8 languages).

name: Mozilla Common Voice - Kinyarwanda
notes: One of the largest Common Voice language sets ever (2,383 hrs reported at the 20k-hour release, built largely via Digital Umuganda community drives); CC0 read speech, crowd-recorded so quality varies.

name: QASR (QCRI Aljazeera Speech Resource)
notes: ~2,000 h of Aljazeera broadcasts with multi-layer annotation (transcripts, speaker ID, dialect, punctuation, code-switching); largest transcribed Arabic broadcast corpus, request-gated via Google Form.

name: SALAN: A Massive ASR Dataset for the Languages of Niger
notes: By far the largest Sahel ASR resource: 2,000+ hours across eight Nigerien languages from radio and community recordings, with trained models promised as public. First reported speech data for Buduma, Tubu and Gourmanchema; check the paper for the actual release location.

name: African Voices (Data Science Nigeria / Gates Foundation)
notes: 1,900 audio hours / 1.9 m transcribed sentences; built by Data Science Nigeria with Awarri, NITI and Univ. of Ibadan Linguistics; free registration, filterable metadata, chunked download.

name: NaijaVoices
notes: ~600 h per language, 1.9M+ sentences, 5,000+ speakers with gender and age balance, nine batches of ~167 h. Non-commercial licence with a separate commercial waiver via Lanfrica membership. By far the largest open Igbo/Hausa/Yoruba speech corpus (arXiv 2505.20564).

name: NaijaVoices (project download portal)
notes: Official project portal for the same 1,800-hour corpus, with batched downloads and a compressed 84 GB variant.

name: Orinode Nigerian speech corpus
notes: 1,500+ h of crowdsourced, commercially-consented Nigerian speech including deliberate code-switching; corpus is proprietary, though a 15,000-sentence code-switch text corpus is open-sourced. Contributors paid above local rates.

name: NCHLT Auxiliary Speech Data (Aux1 + Aux2, all 11 languages)
notes: Aux1 (780.6 h / 2,220 speakers) + Aux2 (640.7 h / 1,181 speakers) of previously unreleased NCHLT recordings in varied acoustic conditions; more than doubles NCHLT for several languages. Per-language sets are individual SADiLaR handles.

name: Afrivoice_V2 (Digital Umuganda)
notes: 261,923 clips, 83.2 GB: Kirundi 380.92 h (agriculture, education), Ndau 326.59 h (education, health), Northern Ndebele 442.96 h, Oshiwambo 242.29 h (agriculture, finance). First substantial open speech data in existence for Ndau, Oshiwambo and Kirundi. Gated: requires sharing contact info.

name: WAXAL / WaxalNLP (Google Research Africa multilingual African speech corpus)
notes: Largest new open African speech release (21-27 languages depending on count, ~1.25k transcribed ASR hours + studio TTS); collected by African institutions via picture-description prompts, so natural and code-switched. West African coverage includes Fula and Hausa; check per-language configs.

name: WAXAL corpus paper
notes: Paper documenting WAXAL collection (Jan 2021-Mar 2024), per-language splits and the 72-speaker community TTS recording protocol.

name: MGB-2 (Arabic Multi-Genre Broadcast Challenge 2)
notes: 1,200 h of Aljazeera TV with lightly-supervised transcripts spanning MSA plus Egyptian, Gulf, Levantine and North African dialects; requires signing the QCRI-Aljazeera licence.

name: Ethio-ASR (models + recipes for joint ASR and LID)
notes: Multilingual Ethiopian ASR+language-ID models trained on the WAXAL Ethiopian subset; the paper (arXiv 2603.23654) is the best single survey of Ethiopian speech resources. Code at github.com/badrex/Ethio-ASR.

name: AfriSpeech african-speech-ipa
notes: Same audio as african-speech-public_v1 re-transcribed to IPA for 141 languages, 775,799 clips; per-language hours for my cluster: Kabuverdianu 9.05, Loma 9.01, Kpelle 8.54, Krio 8.47, Baoulé 8.08, Bassa 6.07, Liberian English 5.79, Kisi 3.96, Attié 1.40.

name: LugandaSoloSpeech_1K
notes: ~1,000 hrs of UNLABELLED Luganda audio scraped from radio shows and YouTube (43.8 GB MP3, 16 kHz); for self-supervised pretraining, quality varies from clean to music-over-speech.

name: MASC (Massive Arabic Speech Corpus)
notes: 1,000 h at 16 kHz crawled from 700+ YouTube channels, MSA plus 20+ dialects; North African coverage is thin (LinTO reports only ~3 h of Tunisian) but it is a common pre-training pool.

name: African Next Voices - Kikuyu
notes: 183 hrs scripted + 571 hrs unscripted, 174k audio files (~215 GB); gated behind a contact-sharing form; by far the biggest Kikuyu speech resource.

name: Congolese Speech Radio Corpus (CSRC) - original release
notes: Untranscribed radio speech for self-supervised pretraining: Lingala 274.1h, Swahili 191.1h, Kikongo 174.4h, Tshiluba 112.8h (Data in Brief paper).

name: VoxLingua107
notes: YouTube-mined spoken language ID corpus, 107 languages. African per-language hours: Malagasy 109, Hausa 106, Somali 103, Yoruba 94, Lingala 90, Amharic 81, Swahili 64, Arabic 59, Shona 30. Labels come from video metadata so they are noisy and there are no transcripts - but it is a large, permissively licensed pool of real in-the-wild African audio usable for pre-training and LID.

name: Aswat
notes: 732 h of clean multi-genre Arabic speech assembled for self-supervised pre-training (wav2vec / data2vec); dialect breakdown not published, access via authors.

name: African Next Voices - Dholuo
notes: 195 hrs scripted + 528 hrs unscripted, ~138k clips; gated access form.

name: Mozilla Common Voice - Swahili
notes: 719 hrs reported at the CV v9 milestone, grown through the Mozilla/GIZ Kiswahili collection drive across Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda; later versions are larger.

name: BantuLanguagesInitiative/CSRC
notes: HF repackaging of the radio corpus into 97,779 quality-scored 4-50s segments; unlabelled, no diarisation, ideal for SSL pretraining.

name: Niger-Mali Audio Collection (Studio Kalangou / Studio Tamani)
notes: 671 h raw / 641 h auto-segmented radio audio including 224 h of Tamasheq and 111 h of Nigerien French - unlabelled, intended for self-supervised pre-training; the largest Tuareg audio pool in existence and also a source of West/North African accented French.

name: SADA (Saudi Audio Dataset for Arabic)
notes: 668 h from 57 Saudi Broadcasting Authority TV shows; Saudi dialects are out of this cluster's scope but the corpus explicitly includes Egyptian (and Yemeni/Levantine) segments, so it is a usable pan-Arabic set with Egyptian coverage. Roughly 1/3 clean, 1/3 noisy, 1/3 with music.

name: Luhya ASR Data (Digital Divide Data) - 642h
notes: Large multi-dialect Luhya corpus (Bukusu and other varieties) with speaker/age/gender metadata; smaller 50h and dialect-specific subsets also published by the same org.

name: AFVoices — African Next Voices Bambara
notes: Largest Bambara speech corpus ever released: spontaneous speech collected across southern Mali (agriculture, health, education) under the Gates-funded African Next Voices programme, with human-corrected and model-annotated subsets.

name: CLEAR Global synthetic Hausa voice data (XTTS / YourTTS)
notes: Synthetic (TTS-generated) Hausa speech released to augment ASR training at <1% the cost of real data; hosted on huggingface.co/CLEAR-Global. Synthetic, so use as augmentation only.

name: Hausa-Synthetic-ASR-Dataset-XTTS
notes: 574 h / 89 GB of fully synthetic 24 kHz Hausa speech from a fine-tuned XTTS-v2 over GPT-4o-generated text; useful for ASR augmentation only, not a natural-speech corpus.

name: Chichewa Synthetic ASR Dataset (CLEAR Global)
notes: 550h of 24kHz Chichewa audio synthesised with a fine-tuned YourTTS model over LLM-generated text; largest Chichewa 'speech' set by far but fully synthetic, non-commercial, and gated behind an acknowledgement.

name: Nemotron 3.5 Kenyan-language adaptation (data recipe)
notes: No new data, but publishes the post-cleaning usable hours of the ANV sets (Kikuyu 182.3, Dholuo 206.9, Kalenjin 151.3 hrs train) and the cleaning rules - the best guide to what is actually trainable in ANV.

name: African Next Voices - Kalenjin
notes: 122 hrs scripted + 399 hrs unscripted, ~99.5k clips.

name: Waxal Multilingual speech-data (chatbot-crowdsourced Wolof)
notes: Earlier (pre-Google) Waxal project: speech crowd-sourced over WhatsApp/Twilio, linguist-transcribed; large raw pool but tiny transcribed portion.

name: African Next Voices - Maasai
notes: 51 hrs scripted + 454 hrs unscripted (~62k clips) - the only large Maa/Maasai speech corpus in existence.

name: African Next Voices - Somali (Kenya)
notes: 118 hrs scripted + 384 hrs unscripted from Kenyan Somali speakers (~94k clips); distinct from Somalia-based Somali corpora.

name: GhanaNLP twi-health-asr-gemini-500hrs
notes: ~500 h / 59.3 k rows of health-domain Twi audio with Gemini-assisted transcriptions — large but machine-transcribed, so treat labels as silver-standard.

name: UGSpeechData (Science Data Bank deposit)
notes: Archival deposit of the transcribed portion (100 h per language) described in the Data in Brief paper.

name: LinTO Augmented Audio Dataset for Tunisian Arabic (ar-tn-augmented)
notes: 466 h produced by voice-conversion augmentation of the 93 h base set - speaker diversity is synthetic, so use for training robustness rather than as new natural data.

name: Swahili Speech 400hr (Kenyan domains)
notes: ~400 hrs, 385 voices recorded in Nairobi across government services, agriculture, education, health and finance; 64.5k train / 4k validation clips with tagged transcripts.

name: EthioSpeech (ELRA-S0494)
notes: Largest licensed Horn corpus: 68h Amharic, 62h Tigrinya, 70h Oromo, 56h Somali, 68h Afar, 68h Sidama, ~200 speakers per language aged 18-40; the only substantial Afar and Sidamo ASR data anywhere.

name: EthioSpeech (ELRA-S0494)
notes: ISLRN 886-456-351-764-8. Over 391 h of read speech across six Ethiopian languages with roughly 200 speakers each - the largest single licensable Horn-of-Africa speech corpus. Paid ELRA licence.

name: Shaip South African English Speech Dataset
notes: Off-the-shelf licensable catalogue item: 132h37 dual-channel 8 kHz call-centre agent-customer conversations (324 spk) plus 245h23 mono 16 kHz media/podcast audio (687 spk). The largest accented-SA-English commercial set found.

name: Nigerian English Speech Recognition Corpus (Mobile)
notes: 357.4 h of mobile-recorded Nigerian English from 206 gender-balanced speakers, 16 kHz/16-bit, 95% sentence accuracy; the largest commercially licensable Nigerian-English ASR corpus found.

name: IARPA Babel Swahili Language Pack (IARPA-babel202b-v1.0d)
notes: Conversational plus scripted telephone speech collected 2012-2014 in the Nairobi dialect region, with transcripts; built by Appen for IARPA Babel. Still the largest transcribed conversational telephone Swahili corpus. LDC membership or non-member licence fee required.

name: CORAA v1.1
notes: 290.77h multi-project Portuguese ASR corpus - but BRAZILIAN varieties only, no African Portuguese. Included because it is the usual (imperfect) starting point for Mozambican/Angolan Portuguese ASR transfer.

name: AfriVox-v2
notes: Aggregated 'in-the-wild' spontaneous ASR benchmark over 24 African languages, ~251 h from three sources (AFN ~100 h, Waxal ~69.5 h, AfriVox v1 ~81.5 h), annotated across 10 deployment domains. CC-BY-4.0 and unscripted, which makes it unusually useful for realistic evaluation. Intron also publishes afrivox-transcribe, afrivox-translate and NigBench-MAMAI-Speech-QA.

name: Zambezi Voice (arXiv paper)
notes: Paper documenting collection sprint from Zambian TV/radio and YouTube, with per-language hours and self-supervised baselines.

name: Zambezi Voice (project release)
notes: UNZA Speech Lab multilingual Zambian corpus: ~80h labelled (Bemba 26-28, Nyanja 25, Tonga 22, Lozi 6) plus ~168h segmented unlabelled radio audio incl. Lunda; the single most important Zambian resource beyond Bemba.

name: Ethiopian Amharic Speech Recognition Corpus (Mobile) - DataOceanAI
notes: 220M/180F speakers recorded on mobile phones in quiet office/home settings, 16 kHz 16-bit, claimed 95% sentence accuracy rate; largest commercial Amharic offering found.

name: IARPA Babel Zulu Language Pack (IARPA-babel206b-v0.1e)
notes: Conversational and scripted telephone Zulu with transcripts, developed by Appen for IARPA Babel. Also excerpted in the LDC Spoken Language Sampler (5th release), which is a cheap way to inspect it before licensing.

name: IARPA Babel Igbo Language Pack (IARPA-babel306b-v2.0c)
notes: Conversational and scripted telephone Igbo collected 2014-2015 with transcripts. Largest transcribed conversational Igbo corpus; dwarfs Common Voice Igbo (19 h).

name: IARPA Babel Amharic Language Pack (IARPA-babel307b-v1.0b, LDC2019S22)
notes: 204h of conversational + scripted telephone speech across three Ethiopian dialect regions, ~75% transcribed in both Ge'ez script and romanisation; the only large telephone-channel Horn corpus. BABEL has no Tigrinya, Somali or Oromo pack.

name: AfriSpeech-200
notes: The reference African-accented English ASR corpus: 200 h (173.4 train / 8.74 dev / 18.77 test), 2,463 speakers, 120 accents, 13 countries, clinical plus general domain. Nigeria 142.4 h, South Africa 22.7 h, Kenya 20.9 h. Non-commercial licence. Built by Intron Health to expose racial/accent bias in commercial ASR.

name: AfriSpeech-200 (negative result for the Horn)
notes: NEGATIVE RESULT for this cluster: the flagship African-accented English corpus covers 120 accents from 13 countries but explicitly excludes Ethiopia, Eritrea, Djibouti and Somalia. No Ethiopian-English or Somali-accented-English speech dataset was found anywhere.

name: Kinyarwanda cleaned verified test/train sets (10-200 hr tiers)
notes: Human-verified cleaned Kinyarwanda subsets released at 10/20/100/200 hr tiers for low-resource ASR ablations; derived from Common Voice.

name: BIG-C (ACL 2023 paper)
notes: Paper release with ASR, MT and speech-translation baselines; documents collection protocol and speaker demographics.

name: BIG-C (Bemba Image Grounded Conversations)
notes: Lacuna-funded multimodal Bemba corpus: 92,000+ transcribed spoken utterances (>180h) of image-grounded dialogue with English translations; largest Bemba speech resource and usable for ASR, speech translation and TTS.

name: Mozilla Common Voice Spontaneous Speech v4.0 - African languages
notes: Newer unscripted modality: contributors answer open questions, community transcribes. African languages dominate it: Ruuli 17.8h, Rutooro 16.8h, Bukusu 15.9h, Thur 15.4h, Lendu 15.1h, Konzo 14.9h, Nubi 14.0h, Amba 13.6h, Kenyi 12.4h, Kuku 11.8h, Chiga 11.7h, Basaa 5.4h, plus small Tashlhiyt/Sena/Tudaga/Shimaore/Lango sets. Rare source of genuinely spontaneous speech for Ugandan/DRC minority languages; CC0.

name: djelia/bambara-audio
notes: 123 GB of YouTube-sourced Bambara audio, denoised (Resemble AI) and diarized (pyannote), with a semi-annotated subset transcribed by Djelia's Whisper v1; copyright status of the YouTube source is unresolved.

name: IWSLT 2022 Tunisian Arabic-English dialectal speech translation data (LDC2022E01/E02)
notes: 160 h of Tunisian conversational telephone speech with manual transcripts plus 200k lines of English translation (383 h in the wider LDC collection); free to IWSLT participants after signing an LDC evaluation agreement - largest Tunisian speech resource but not openly redistributable.

name: Kunkado / Kunnafonidilaw ka Cadeau (Bambara radio ASR corpus)
notes: 118,925 segments from Malian radio, 33.5h human-reviewed; deliberately keeps code-switching, disfluencies and noise, and models trained on it beat larger clean corpora.

name: Makerere Radio Speech Corpus (Luganda)
notes: 20 hrs human-transcribed radio speech plus 135 hrs untranscribed multi-speaker audio, 16 kHz mono; cleaned and uncleaned transcripts with [laughter]/[um] annotation (LREC 2022).

name: Makerere Radio Speech Corpus (paper record)
notes: LREC paper documenting collection from Ugandan radio for agricultural radio monitoring; describes the wider Makerere radio-monitoring pipeline.

name: GO AI Corp Mooré speech Bible corpus
notes: 84,510 sentence-aligned Mooré segments (76h from bible.com + ~70h from jw.org) force-aligned with MMS; by far the largest Mooré speech resource but non-commercial, gated and with unresolved upstream rights.

name: Financial Inclusion Speech Dataset (Ashesi University / Nokwary, Lacuna Fund)
notes: ~38 h Akuapem Twi, ~30 h Asante Twi, ~39 h Fante, ~40 h Ga; ~200 speakers per variety, ~130 sentences each from Wizard-of-Oz banking prompts. CC-BY-4.0 makes this the most commercially usable Ghanaian ASR corpus.

name: nicolingua-0003 West African Radio Corpus - SLR105
notes: 17,090 x 30 s clips sampled from six Guinean radio stations, unlabelled/untranscribed (code-switched French + 9 Guinean languages, with music and phone-in calls). Built for unsupervised representation learning; the only open Guinean broadcast corpus.

name: Kallaama - SLR151
notes: 125 h of transcribed agricultural-domain speech in Senegal's three biggest languages, 35 h with verified transcripts. Lacuna-Fund-era project (funded 2023); the largest open Sereer and Pulaar speech resource.

name: Kallaama speech dataset (GitHub/Zenodo release)
notes: Primary repo with transcription conventions and splits; Zenodo DOI mirror at zenodo.org/records/10892569.

name: BOLT CTS CALLFRIEND CALLHOME Egyptian Arabic Audio (LDC2025S09)
notes: 116.32 h (89.16 train / 5.58 dev / 21.58 eval) from 274 speakers; consolidates CALLHOME, CALLFRIEND and HUB5 Egyptian audio and adds 92 previously unreleased calls - the largest single Egyptian telephone-speech release.

name: TWB Voice 1.0 (Hausa, Kanuri, Shuwa Arabic)
notes: CLEAR Global community-collected read speech: 54.4h Hausa, 44.6h Kanuri, 12.5h Shuwa Arabic (approved portions). Recorded in Nigeria but the only sizeable Kanuri ASR corpus, directly relevant to Diffa/Niger Kanuri.

name: Moroccan Arabic Speech Recognition Corpus (King-ASR-152)
notes: 110 h of mobile-phone recordings from 100 balanced speakers (16 kHz/16-bit) in quiet office/home conditions; the largest Darija ASR corpus available at all, but commercial-only.

name: b1n1yam/Sagalee (Addis AI redistribution)
notes: 53.6k-row packaging of Sagalee used to train Addis AI's open Amharic/Oromo ASR models (Shook family, ~2,000h Amharic audio).

name: KasuleTrevor/Lingala_100hrs
notes: 23.5k train/dev/test utterances merging AfriVoice, LRSC and FLEURS Lingala - the largest ready-to-train transcribed Lingala set.

name: Luganda Bible Audio 100Hrs
notes: Luganda scripture narration (incl. a 24 hr New Testament block) segmented for ASR/TTS; licence not stated, derived from religious recordings.

name: Sagalee (OpenSLR SLR157)
notes: First large open-source Oromo ASR corpus (ICASSP 2025), read speech in clean and noisy conditions; non-commercial licence.

name: turiabu/Sagalee (HuggingFace)
notes: HF distribution of Sagalee; code and Kaldi/ESPnet recipes at github.com/turinaf/sagalee.

name: Chichewa Speech Dataset (Speech-data)
notes: 94h across 740 files with 52/48 female/male balance and speakers aged 18-50+ drawn from Malawi, Zambia, Mozambique and Zimbabwe; the largest claimed natural Chichewa audio set, but the HF viewer exposes only one row so verify the actual files.

name: LinTO Tunisian Arabic audio dataset
notes: Largest openly licensed Tunisian Arabic ASR set: 92h56 raw (466h with voice-conversion augmentation, released separately as linto-dataset-audio-ar-tn-augmented), aggregating TunSwitch, MASC-Tunisian and TV/radio material. Excludes non-commercial TARIC.

name: BibleTTS
notes: Highest-quality open African TTS corpus: single-speaker, studio, 48 kHz, verse-aligned, commercial-friendly licence. Six aligned languages plus four further unaligned languages. Produced by Biblica/Open.Bible with Masakhane and CMU collaborators (Interspeech 2022).

name: BibleTTS paper release (Masakhane / Coqui)
notes: Project site with per-language download links and alignment recipes; Lingala is one of six aligned languages.

name: SpeechTaxi
notes: 80 h / 28 languages of Bible-verse audio labelled with semantic topic classes; 8 of the 28 languages are African (derived from the same Biblica/Open.Bible-style recordings as BibleTTS). Built for semantic speech classification but the aligned verse audio is reusable for ASR/TTS.

name: Digital Divide Data Somali ASR Subset (68 hours)
notes: Best open Somali ASR corpus: ~256k rows with speaker IDs, dialect labels (Maxaatiri/Maay), domain and theme tags, and speaker age/gender. Collected with Kenyan Somali speakers; also on Mozilla Data Collective as ddd-kenya-somali-68hrs-asr.

name: AfriSpeech-Countries
notes: 21,581 clips / 67.73 h assembled as a country-stratified accent-robustness test set (no train split), aggregating Intron's parliamentary, names and AfriSpeech-200 collections across 7 regions including North Africa. Read + conversational, clinical/legal/general.

name: Zambezi Voice unlabelled Bemba audio
notes: Segmented Bemba broadcast audio without transcripts, complementing BembaSpeech and BIG-C.

name: Rwandan Kinyarwanda nonstandard (disordered) speech v1.0
notes: 14,739 samples from 61 Rwandan speakers with stuttering, dysarthria, dysphonia, phonological disorders; gated by CDLI terms and conditions.

name: FFSTC-2
notes: Extended Fongbe corpus: 61 h / 33.7 k rows with validated French translations, usable for Fongbe ASR and Fongbe-French speech translation. The single largest open Fon speech resource.

name: FFSTC-2 (IWSLT 2025 paper)
notes: Publication describing the FFSTC extension, models and benchmark.

name: CALLHOME Egyptian Arabic Speech (LDC97S45)
notes: 120 unscripted Cairene Arabic telephone calls up to 30 min each; the historical foundation of Egyptian Arabic ASR and still a standard eval set. LDC user agreement, fee-based.

name: Zambezi Voice unlabelled Tonga audio
notes: Largest unlabelled block in Zambezi Voice; Tonga is also spoken across the border in Zimbabwe so this transfers.

name: NCHLT English Speech Corpus
notes: Core NCHLT wideband read-speech corpus (~56 h 'clean' per language) with orthographic transcriptions and an 8-speaker test set; the single most important open ASR resource for this language.

notes: Core NCHLT wideband read-speech corpus (~56 h 'clean' per language) with orthographic transcriptions and an 8-speaker test set; the single most important open ASR resource for this language.

notes: Core NCHLT wideband read-speech corpus (~56 h 'clean' per language) with orthographic transcriptions and an 8-speaker test set; the single most important open ASR resource for this language.

notes: Core NCHLT wideband read-speech corpus (~56 h 'clean' per language) with orthographic transcriptions and an 8-speaker test set; the single most important open ASR resource for this language.

name: NCHLT Sepedi Speech Corpus
notes: Core NCHLT wideband read-speech corpus (~56 h 'clean' per language) with orthographic transcriptions and an 8-speaker test set; the single most important open ASR resource for this language.

notes: Core NCHLT wideband read-speech corpus (~56 h 'clean' per language) with orthographic transcriptions and an 8-speaker test set; the single most important open ASR resource for this language.

notes: Core NCHLT wideband read-speech corpus (~56 h 'clean' per language) with orthographic transcriptions and an 8-speaker test set; the single most important open ASR resource for this language.

notes: Core NCHLT wideband read-speech corpus (~56 h 'clean' per language) with orthographic transcriptions and an 8-speaker test set; the single most important open ASR resource for this language.

name: NCHLT Speech Corpus HuggingFace mirrors (danielshaps/nchlt_speech_*)
notes: Loader-ready HuggingFace repackaging of all 11 NCHLT language corpora (nchlt_speech_afr/eng/nbl/nso/sot/ssw/tsn/tso/ven/xho/zul); easiest route to the NCHLT audio.

name: NCHLT Tshivenda Speech Corpus
notes: Core NCHLT wideband read-speech corpus (~56 h 'clean' per language) with orthographic transcriptions and an 8-speaker test set; the single most important open ASR resource for this language.

name: NCHLT Xitsonga Speech Corpus
notes: Core NCHLT wideband read-speech corpus (~56 h 'clean' per language) with orthographic transcriptions and an 8-speaker test set; the single most important open ASR resource for this language.

name: AfriSwitch
notes: 16,602 utterances with 69,928 code-switch events across 14 African languages paired with English, plus per-utterance CMI and switch-point metrics. The only continent-scale code-switched African speech benchmark; a companion AfriSwitchCare covers healthcare code-switching.

name: TWB Voice 1.0 - Hausa (Mozilla Data Collective listing)
notes: Mozilla Data Collective mirror/listing of the Hausa portion of TWB Voice.

name: ADI-20 - Mauritanian dialect split
notes: ADI-20 guarantees at least 53 h of training audio per dialect including Mauritanian, so its Mauritanian manifest is the largest identified pool of Hassaniya audio - dialect-labelled, not transcribed.

name: Dataset.ET Amharic Speech v0.2.0
notes: Crowdsourced Ethiopian community corpus: 16,866 recordings from 493 contributors, released 30 Aug 2026 under CC-BY-4.0.

name: snapwre/amharic-speech (HuggingFace release of Dataset.ET Amharic)
notes: 16.9k FLAC clips at 16 kHz with train/val/test splits and duration/silence metadata; the easiest large open Amharic ASR download.

name: Algeria Arabic General Conversation Speech Dataset
notes: ~50 h of spontaneous two-speaker Algerian Darja dialogue with verified transcripts and speaker metadata; commercial licence. One of the only substantial Algerian-dialect offerings from any vendor.

name: BULBasaa: Bilingual Basaa-French Speech Corpus
notes: ~50h of Basaa (radio + elicited picture-task + dictionary recordings) with ~10h phonetically transcribed and French re-speaking/translation; distributed via ELDA - the single most substantial Cameroonian indigenous-language speech corpus.

name: Egyptian Arabic General Conversation Speech Dataset
notes: 50 h of unscripted peer-to-peer Egyptian dialogue, 70 speakers across Egyptian regions, stereo 16 kHz WAV with human-verified transcripts (<5% WER claimed); commercial licence, free sample available.

name: ÌròyìnSpeech
notes: 42 h recorded in-house by 80 volunteers plus 6 h validated via Mozilla Common Voice; multi-purpose (TTS demonstrated from 5 h, ASR WER 21.5).

name: ÌròyìnSpeech (arXiv preprint release)
notes: Preprint describing the same Yoruba corpus; useful for the news/TED text-source documentation.

name: OOOK Sudanese dialect collection (OOOK-Full-Dataset / OOOK-Eval)
notes: 18,883 clips (~45.3 h) drawn from the Sudanese portion of ADI17 across 30 channels; ~909 clips (~2 h) manually transcribed by 15 native annotators as OOOK-Eval, the rest used for self-training pseudo-labels.

name: TWB Voice 1.0 - Kanuri (Mozilla Data Collective listing)
notes: Mozilla Data Collective listing of the Kanuri portion of TWB Voice.

name: Ugandan Luganda nonstandard (disordered) speech v1.0
notes: 8,137 samples, 59 Kampala speakers with speech impairments, professionally transcribed and anonymised.

name: oza75/bible-bambara-audio
notes: 48 kHz verse-aligned Bambara New/Old Testament audio scraped from Bible.is; high fidelity single-speaker so good for TTS, but redistribution licence is unclear (FCBH terms).

name: Ugandan English nonstandard (disordered) speech v1.0
notes: 7,251 samples of Ugandan English from 59 speakers with impairments; speaker- and phrase-disjoint splits.

name: NaijaS2ST
notes: Multi-accent parallel speech benchmark for speech-to-speech/speech-to-text translation covering Nigerian Pidgin plus Nigerian- and British-accented English; ~24-61h per language after QC.

name: FarmerlineML TTS_yor_36h
notes: 36 h / 4.1 GB Yoruba TTS+ASR set from Farmerline (Ghana); gated behind contact-sharing but CC-BY-4.0 and used to train their ASR_yoruba_AI4G model.

name: AfriSpeech-Parliament
notes: Test-only set of 8,068 manually transcribed parliamentary clips from four African parliaments; noisy multi-speaker real-world accented English.

name: Rwandan English nonstandard (disordered) speech v1.0
notes: 7,592 samples of Rwandan-accented English from 44 speakers with speech impairments; terms-and-conditions gate, re-identification forbidden.

name: Kenyan Swahili nonstandard (disordered) speech v1.0
notes: 5,535 samples from 52 Nairobi speakers with cerebral palsy, Parkinson's, autism, stroke, stuttering etc; SLP-transcribed, dual-pass QA; UCL GDI Hub / Centre for Digital Language Inclusion.

name: Kenyan English Nonstandard Speech v1.0
notes: 5,998 samples of Kenyan-accented English from 52 speakers with speech impairments (cerebral palsy, Parkinson's, stroke, stuttering etc.), double-transcribed by SLPs. Openly licensed and by far the largest single-country Kenyan English audio release; atypical speech, so pair with AfriSpeech for typical-speech modelling.

name: FFSTC (LREC-COLING 2024 record)
notes: Peer-reviewed publication record for FFSTC with the corpus construction details.

name: FFSTC: Fongbe to French Speech Translation Corpus
notes: 31 h (20/7/4 train/dev/test) of Fongbe speech with French transcriptions from 20 volunteers aged 20-40; the first public Fongbe speech-translation corpus and the backbone Beninese resource.

name: jeli-asr (Bambara griot narrations, RobotsMali)
notes: 33.6k utterances of jeli (griot) narration with Bambara transcriptions and parallel French translations; also supports speech translation. Audio quality varies (live performance).

name: MosesJoshuaCoker/30_hours_krio_voice
notes: 2.21 GB gated Krio speech set advertised as ~30 hours; README empty and licence undeclared, must accept sharing conditions.

name: AfricanVoices (Lingala TTS corpus)
notes: CMU/neulab curation of Open.Bible Lingala into a clean TTS corpus with Festvox recipes; 27.5h is the second-largest Lingala TTS resource.

name: Corpus of Multilingual Code-switched Soap Opera Speech (SABC soap opera corpus)
notes: Manually segmented/transcribed speech from 626 SABC soap-opera episodes; 26.9 h total, of which the LREC-2018 release is 14.3 h balanced over English-isiZulu (5.45 h), English-isiXhosa (3.14 h), English-Setswana (2.86 h) and English-Sesotho (2.83 h). The reference code-switching ASR benchmark for Southern Bantu languages.

name: African Speech Technology isiXhosa Speech Corpus
notes: isiXhosa telephone speech, orthographically and phonetically transcribed. From the 2000-2004 African Speech Technology project (fixed + mobile telephone, orthographic and phonetic transcription).

name: CALLFRIEND Egyptian Arabic Second Edition (LDC2019S04)
notes: ~25 h across 60 unscripted Egyptian Arabic telephone calls (1990s collection, re-released 2019); originally built for language-ID research.

name: TEDxTN
notes: 25 h from 130 speakers of TEDx Tunisia talks with professional Tunisian transcripts plus French and English translations; first open code-switched Tunisian-to-English speech-translation corpus.

name: Zambezi Voice Nyanja labelled subset
notes: Transcribed Zambian Nyanja (mutually intelligible with Malawian Chichewa/Chewa) read speech; the largest labelled Nyanja set found.

name: Ethiopian Amharic Conversational Speech Recognition Corpus (Mobile) - DataOceanAI
notes: 10M/10F natural two-party conversations on mobile phones; rare conversational (rather than read) Amharic data. A matching Amharic pronunciation lexicon is also sold.

name: BembaSpeech
notes: 14,438 read utterances (>24h) from Bemba literature, radio/TV and YouTube transcripts; the first and still the reference open Bemba ASR corpus.

name: BembaSpeech (LREC 2022 paper release)
notes: Peer-reviewed description of BembaSpeech with DeepSpeech/wav2vec2 baselines; cite this for hours and splits.

name: ARTPARK-IISc Vaani (Bhojpuri portion)
notes: ADJACENT (Indian Bhojpuri, not Mauritian): 23.78 transcribed hours of Bhojpuri inside a 2,041-hour 59-language district-sampled corpus; best open starting point for Mauritian Bhojpuri transfer learning.

name: Design of a Tigrinya Language Speech Corpus for Speech Recognition
notes: Phonetically balanced read Tigrinya (17.57h train / 2.30h adapt / 3.30h test) covering Northern and Southern dialects in office/street/in-car noise; authors intended third-party distribution but no public link was ever published.

name: African Accented French (HuggingFace mirror)
notes: 11,386 clips (9,401 train / 1,985 test) - ready-to-load mirror of SLR57 for HF pipelines.

name: African Accented French (OpenSLR SLR57)
languages_clean: French (Congo, The Democratic Republic of the)
notes: Three collections: Yaounde 2003 (84 Cameroonian speakers), CA16 2016 (125 speakers recorded at a UN exercise in Gabon, multiple Central African nationalities) and Niamey 2015; fully transcribed - the core accented-French resource for this cluster.

name: Large Vocabulary Read Speech Corpora for Four Ethiopian Languages (LREC 2020)
notes: Parallel-design read corpora with baseline WERs 31-38%; the first published Wolaytta ASR corpus. Distribution channel not stated in the paper (overlaps the ELRA EthioSpeech family).

name: African Speech Technology English-English Speech Corpus
notes: White/L1 South African English telephone speech. From the 2000-2004 African Speech Technology project (fixed + mobile telephone, orthographic and phonetic transcription).

name: Amharic Speech Corpus: A 20-Hour Multi-Speaker Dataset for ASR (Addis Ababa University)
notes: 10,850 utterances, 16 kHz mono WAV with time-aligned CSV transcriptions from AAU Computer Science; download needs an IEEE DataPort subscription.

name: ALFFA Amharic (OpenSLR SLR25)
notes: The de facto baseline open Amharic ASR corpus (1.0 GB read speech from the Addis Ababa University corpus) with Kaldi recipes; mirrored from the ALFFA_PUBLIC git repo.

name: An Amharic Speech Corpus for Large Vocabulary Continuous Speech Recognition (Abate, Menzel & Tafila)
notes: The original AAU Amharic read-speech corpus (INTERSPEECH 2005) that underlies the ALFFA Amharic release; the canonical citation for Amharic ASR.

name: hadamard-2/alffa-amharic (HuggingFace mirror of ALFFA Amharic)
notes: Ready-to-load HF port of the ALFFA Amharic read-speech set; convenient for fine-tuning Whisper/wav2vec2.

name: Zambezi Voice unlabelled Lunda audio
notes: Only known Lunda speech dataset of any size; untranscribed, so needs annotation before supervised ASR.

name: flagship-ai/ghomala-spoken-bible
notes: 260 New Testament chapters of Ghomala' (Bamileke) with verse-level parallel Ghomala'/French/English text - 23,846 rows; enables ASR, TTS and speech translation for a Bamileke language.

name: Isma/alffa_wolof (HuggingFace mirror of ALFFA Wolof)
notes: Convenient HF mirror (2.07 GB) of the ALFFA Wolof set; used to train wav2vec2/MMS Wolof models.

name: CMU Wilderness Multilingual Speech Dataset — MNKBSG (Mandinka)
notes: 18:30:28 / 10,668 aligned utterances; this is Gambian/Senegalese Mandinka, only a close relative of the Manding 'Mandingo' spoken in Liberia and Sierra Leone — use with caution.

name: Afaan Oromo Text to Speech Synthesis dataset (Mendeley mpy85ns82z)
notes: 8,076 single-male-speaker WAV clips at 22.05 kHz with raw and normalised transcriptions (news, non-fiction, Oromo Bible) - the best single-speaker TTS set for any Horn language.

name: IWSLT 2022 Tamasheq-French speech translation corpus
notes: 17 h clean (19 h full) / 5,829 utterances of Studio Kalangou radio in Tamasheq with French translations; >99% male speakers. Collected in Niger but the Tuareg dialect continuum extends into southern Algeria and Libya, so this is the main resource for Tuareg/Tamasheq speech in this cluster.

name: Egyptian-ASR-MGB-3 (HuggingFace mirror of MGB-3)
notes: Loader/mirror for MGB-3 on the Hub; audio still has to be obtained under the MGB licence.

name: MGB-3 (Egyptian dialectal Arabic, in-the-wild YouTube)
notes: ~16 h from ~80 YouTube programmes (comedy, cooking, sport, science) with 4 independent manual transcriptions each; the standard Egyptian dialect ASR benchmark.

name: Koumankan for Dyula (uvci/koumankan4dyula)
notes: 10,929 Dyula recordings with French and English translations (train/valid/test provided) from Université Virtuelle de Côte d'Ivoire; the main open Dioula ASR/ST corpus and transferable to Bambara.

name: Zambezi Voice unlabelled Lozi audio
notes: Untranscribed Lozi radio audio; labelled Lozi is only ~6h so this is the bulk of available Lozi speech.

name: Global Recordings Network - Lingala
notes: 16 downloadable MP3 programmes (Good News, Look Listen & Live 1-8, Words of Life 1-4, plus health/culture titles, 33-93 min each) with printed scripts available - alignable into TTS/ASR data; also a Brazzaville-Lingala variant page.

name: MGB-5 (Moroccan Darija broadcast/YouTube ASR)
notes: 13 h transcribed from 93 YouTube videos in 7 genres (10.2 h train / 1.3 h dev / 1.4 h test) plus 48 h of untranscribed full videos for adaptation; the only sizeable Darija ASR benchmark.

name: TunSwitch (code-switched Tunisian Arabic speech dataset)
notes: ~13 h transcribed in two parts - TunSwitchCS (Tunisian-French/English code-switched) and TunSwitchTO (Tunisian only) - plus weakly-labelled audio and LM text, in SpeechBrain-ready splits; transcription conventions cover Arabizi/Latin-script Tunisian. The most permissively licensed real Tunisian corpus.

name: ArzEn (Egyptian Arabic-English code-switched speech corpus)
host: ACL Anthology (paper) / German University in Cairo
notes: 12 h of informal interviews with 38 Egyptian bilingual students/staff recorded in a soundproof room; the reference corpus for Egyptian Arabic-English code-switching ASR (extended later as ArzEn-ST for speech translation).

name: ArzEn: Egyptian Arabic-English Code-switching Speech Corpus
notes: 12h / 6,216 utterances of informal bilingual interviews with Egyptian students; the standard Arabic-English code-switch speech benchmark. Widely re-uploaded on HuggingFace as 'arazn' derivatives.

name: ASR-Africa Data Efficiency Benchmark
notes: Makerere AI Lab / Gates-funded benchmark with exactly 1h transcribed audio per language including Shona and Bemba; small but a clean standardised low-resource evaluation set.

name: FLEURS (Few-shot Learning Evaluation of Universal Representations of Speech)
hours: ~12 per language (~250 for the African subset)
notes: 102-language n-way parallel read corpus built on FLORES-101 text; ~10 h train + dev/test per language. The de facto evaluation set for African languages in Whisper, MMS, SeamlessM4T and USM papers. Small per-language volume means it is an eval set, not a training corpus.

name: FLEURS-R
hours: ~12 per language (~250 for the African subset)
notes: Speech-restored (Miipher) version of all 102 FLEURS languages, explicitly released to make FLEURS usable for TTS/speech generation in low-resource languages. Same African language list as FLEURS; audio quality substantially improved over the originals.

name: XTREME-S (FLEURS Lingala subset)
notes: Benchmark wrapper exposing FLEURS Lingala for ASR, speech translation, LID and retrieval tasks.

name: Tunisian_MSA (OpenSLR 46)
notes: 11.2 h of MSA read and prompted speech from 118 speakers near Tunis (plus a 4-speaker 2017 test set), originally for Arabic language-learning pronunciation models; Apache-2.0, so one of the few commercially usable North African corpora.

name: VoxMg
notes: First transcribed Malagasy ASR corpus (3,873 clips): 8.6h validated from VoxLingua107 plus 2.2h from nybaiboly.net Bible/radio audio; baseline WER 33%; no public download link published in the paper.

name: Luganda CallHome-style diarization/transcription set
notes: 380 Luganda telephone conversations with speaker turns, gender labels and transcripts; rare conversational/telephone Luganda data, usable for diarization and ASR.

name: MediaSpeech (French portion)
notes: SLR108 French/Arabic/Turkish/Spanish media speech; not Africa-specific but the closest broadcast-French benchmark against which African-accented French systems are compared.

name: MediaSpeech (OpenSLR SLR108) - French and Arabic
notes: Manually transcribed YouTube media speech test sets. Not African-specific, but the French and Arabic portions are the standard baseline against which African French/Arabic ASR is compared; some Maghreb/African broadcast material is present.

name: TunSwitch (MBZUAI HuggingFace mirror)
notes: HuggingFace mirror of the Zenodo TunSwitch release (a second mirror exists at tunis-ai/TunSwitch); easier to stream than the Zenodo archive.

name: VoiceAfrica (Lanfrica x Meta)
notes: Biggest find for Equatorial Guinea: ~10h each of expert-transcribed conversational Fang and Bube (Bubi) with fillers and code-mixing preserved; 16,383 clips, rich speaker metadata.

name: Zambezi Voice unlabelled Nyanja audio
notes: Segmented untranscribed radio broadcast audio for self-supervised pretraining; pair with the labelled Nyanja set.

name: Dataset.ET Afaan Oromoo Speech v0.1.0
notes: 3,594 crowdsourced recordings from 74 contributors; small but fully open and growing.

name: DODa-audio-dataset (Darija Open Dataset - audio)
notes: 9 h 46 min / 12,743 parallel samples read by 7 contributors (4F/3M), with Darija in both Latin and Arabic script plus English translations, resampled to 16 kHz; MIT licence makes it the most permissive Darija speech set and it already backs several Darija ASR/TTS models.

name: snapwre/afaan-oromoo-speech
notes: HuggingFace mirror of the Dataset.ET Afaan Oromoo crowdsourced speech collection.

name: madoss/faso-speech
notes: Mooré 5:41:41, Fulfulde 2:41:47, Dioula 0:49:45, French 0:12:23; harvested from IPS app-builder literacy pages with source URLs retained.

name: YORÙLECT
notes: ~3 h each in Standard, Ifè and Ìlàje Yoruba over 1,506 parallel sentences (religion/news/TED); the only Yoruba regional-dialect speech resource found.

name: GOAI-MooreSpeechCorpora
notes: Merged, denoised, speaker-labelled Mooré audio-text corpus (5,535 utterances) combining three earlier GO AI collections; the cleanest open-ish Mooré TTS/ASR set.

name: CALLHOME Egyptian Arabic Speech Supplement (LDC2002S37)
notes: 8 h / 20 extra Egyptian telephone calls originally held back for NIST HUB5 evaluation.

name: GlobalPhone Hausa
notes: ~7h train + 1h eval read Hausa plus lexicon, sold via ELDA/ELRA; the ALFFA Hausa recipe depends on buying it. URL not verified so left null.

name: hasiniaina/malagasy-female-speech-dataset
notes: 2,230 female-voice clips (0.99-13.3 s) with normalised Malagasy transcripts; small but the closest thing to a single-speaker Malagasy TTS-style corpus.

name: TARIC (Tunisian Arabic Railway Interaction Corpus)
notes: Task-oriented ticket-counter dialogues recorded at a single Tunis train station; non-commercial, narrow domain, but real spontaneous Tunisian speech.

name: TARIC (Tunisian Arabic Railway Interaction Corpus)
notes: 7 h 25 min of real human-to-human dialogues recorded in Tunisian railway stations, with transcripts and a Tunisian phonetic dictionary; non-commercial licence means downstream projects (e.g. LinTO) cannot redistribute it.

name: TARIC-SLU
notes: TARIC re-annotated end-to-end with dialogue acts and slots for spoken language understanding, with SpeechBrain ASR and SLU baselines; usable as ASR data too.

name: AfriSpeech-Dialog
notes: 50 simulated long-form medical and general dialogues in 11 African English accents; most accent labels are Nigerian minority languages (Idoma, Urhobo, Ijaw, Igala, Isoko, Ebira).

name: AfriSpeech-Dialog
languages: African-accented English (11 accents incl. Hausa, Yoruba, Igbo, Swahili, Sesotho L1)
notes: 50 two-speaker dialogues (20 simulated doctor-patient, 30 general) = 2.07 h medical + 4.93 h general, with timestamped transcripts and speaker labels. Designed for long-form ASR and speaker diarisation evaluation on African-accented English - a gap AfriSpeech-200 (read speech) does not cover.

name: Kenyan-Swahili-Speech (CLEAR Global / Gamayun)
notes: 4,700 prompted read utterances (~6 hrs) from one male Kenyan speaker, from the Gamayun language data kits; small but clean, non-commercial licence.

name: ASR-EgArbCSC: Egyptian Arabic Conversational Speech Corpus
notes: 5.5 h of spontaneous themed dialogue (9 conversations, two speaker pairs) recorded indoors on mobile devices, 16 kHz mono WAV + UTF-8 transcripts; free after sign-in but NC-ND.

name: Lwazi ASR Corpus (Lwazi I)
notes: Narrowband telephone speech (~200 speakers/language, 286-479 min usable per language) for all 11 official languages; the only large open telephone-channel corpus for these languages.

name: Shona_test_5hr
notes: Held-out 5-hour Shona evaluation split used in ASR-Africa benchmarking; handy for comparable WER reporting.

name: Whisper-WOLOF-5-hours-ALFFA (asr-africa) — derived training artefacts
notes: Part of the ASR-Africa benchmark family; documents standardised 5h/19h ALFFA Wolof splits (see also yigagilbert/alffa-wolof-asr-dataset-19hr) useful for reproducible low-resource comparisons.

name: anyantudre/moore-speech-contes (Mooré folk tales)
notes: 5,958 transcribed segments of traditional Mooré storytelling at 16 kHz; gated, non-commercial, but valuable long-form narrative speech.

name: Lisan-Sudanese TTS Dataset (New-Lisan-Sudanese-TTS-Dataset)
notes: 1,880 sentences of SYNTHETIC Sudanese Arabic speech (~4.6 h) with plain and diacritized text, generated to augment ASR training; useful as augmentation data, not as natural-speech ground truth.

name: Lingala-TTS-Dataset (Institute of African Digital Humanities)
notes: 8,572 clips from 1 male + 1 female native speaker on cultural/procedural topics; contains some French code-switching and silence markers to filter.

name: Lingala Read Speech Corpus (LRSC)
notes: Only purpose-built transcribed read-speech corpus for Lingala; 13 male / 19 female speakers, released alongside the Congolese Speech Radio Corpus.

name: WolBanking77 (Wolof banking speech intent classification)
notes: First Wolof spoken-intent dataset: 9,791 text sentences over 77 banking/transport intents plus 4h17 of audio (263 sentences, 10 intents) from 31 sessions; usable for ASR fine-tuning and SLU. Hosted on Kaggle (dsv/11828279).

name: BantuLanguagesInitiative/LRSC
notes: Train/dev/test-split HF mirror of the Lingala read corpus (2,940 utterances, 16kHz, speaker+gender labels).

name: Lwazi II Afrikaans Trajectory Tracking Corpus
notes: Single male speaker, 4 h, built for acoustic trajectory/phonetic modelling; usable as a single-speaker TTS/ASR resource.

name: pyFongbe ASR dataset
notes: ~4 h Fongbe ASR corpus plus Kaldi/Python pipeline from Laleye et al.; the earliest open Fon speech resource.

name: SDN-Dialect-Dataset (Sudanese dialect speech)
notes: 5,362 transcribed recordings (~4 h) from 31 speakers (9F/22M), mostly Khartoum dialect; the primary and for a long time the only transcribed Sudanese Arabic ASR corpus (Mansour & Mukhtar, arXiv:2212.10826).

name: DataOceanAI South African English Multi-style Speech Synthesis Corpus
notes: One male and one female SA English voice talent, 1,562 sentences across voice-assistant, podcast, audiobook and e-learning styles; sold per-licence.

name: Adamawa Fulfulde-TTS-Dataset
notes: 1,303 read-speech recordings (3 h 31 m) with full Fulfulde Latin orthography (ɓ ɗ ƴ ŋ ɲ); Cameroon-primary but the variety is also spoken in north-east Nigeria. Restrictive NOODL licence.

name: Afaan Oromoo Text-to-Speech Dataset (Mendeley hnvkvj589y)
notes: 1,224 clips / 17,559 words recorded by female volunteers at Madda Walabu and Addis Ababa universities; recorded in an uncontrolled environment so some background noise.

name: Towards Digital Preservation of Efik: TTS corpus
notes: 2,632 single-speaker utterances (3.08 h) from Efik novels, folktales and textbooks, native-validated; released under a non-commercial licence on request — the only dedicated Efik speech corpus found.

name: PARADISEC Mauritian Creole field recordings
notes: Field linguistic recordings used as the only real Mauritian Creole ASR data in the COMPUTEL 2026 creole-ASR study (2h30 train + 38 min test after curation). Access via the PARADISEC archive; this paper is the documented route to it.

name: Common Voice Spontaneous Speech (Tachelhit, shi)
notes: Spontaneous Speech corpus v4.0: 2.72 h of open-ended answers from 16 contributors, but only 0.01 h transcribed-and-validated so far; effectively an untranscribed seed corpus for Tashelhit.

name: goaicorp/new-moore-speech-clean (Mooré proverbs)
notes: 1,159 parallel Mooré/French spoken proverbs at 16 kHz with durations; gated but well documented.

name: Lwazi II Proper Name Call Routing Telephone Corpus
notes: Telephone call-routing utterances containing South African proper names.

name: Lwazi II Cross-lingual Proper Name Corpus
notes: Speakers of one language reading proper names from the other three; designed for cross-lingual/name-recognition research.

name: Juba Arabic audio translation dataset
notes: Only 40 long clips (37-200 s) of religious narrative with English translations - essentially the entire public Juba Arabic speech record. Translations, not verbatim transcripts.

name: Kasdi-Merbah University Emotional Database in Arabic Speech (LDC2023S10)
notes: 2 h / 5,000 prompted utterances from 500 Algerian speakers (254F/246M) at Univ. Kasdi Merbah Ouargla, 10 sentences each across sadness, fear, anger, happiness, neutral; 44 kHz FLAC. Built for emotion recognition but usable as Algerian-accented MSA read speech.

name: Somali broadcast radio phone-in corpus (Edinburgh/Stellenbosch semi-supervised ASR)
notes: Captured from Somali radio phone-in programmes for humanitarian ASR; tiny labelled portion (1,300 train + 95 test utterances) with almost no speaker metadata, but shows the radio-harvest route works.

name: Kirundi Open Speech Dataset
notes: The only open Kirundi speech corpus found: 4,737 sentences (2,911 gold Kirundi/French/English) with ~102 recordings (~1.5 hrs) so far, targeting 20+ hrs; community-contributed, 16 kHz mono.

name: GRN audio recordings - Shingazidja (Ngazidja Comorian)
notes: Raw source: 'Good News' (46:22) and 'Lamb of God' (26:12) in Shingazidja with published scripts - roughly 72 minutes of alignable read/narrated Comorian.

name: AwezaMed Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) Test Data
notes: Small real-world-environment ASR test set from CSIR's Voice Computing group for the AwezaMed maternal-health translation app; evaluation-only.

name: CommonLanguage
notes: SpeechBrain's balanced 45.1 h / 43-language language-ID set carved out of Common Voice (1 h per language). Only two of the 43 languages are African (Kinyarwanda, Kabyle) - a good illustration of how Common Voice's African depth is concentrated in a handful of languages.

name: Ehugbo TTS (biblical text-to-speech dataset)
notes: 312 biblical recordings (~1 h) in the Ehugbo/Afikpo Igbo variety by NaijaVoices (Lanfrica Labs) with the Nigeria Bible Translation Trust; rare dialect-level Igbo data.

name: KasuleTrevor Lingala low-resource subsets (1hr / 5hr / 10hr / 20hr)
notes: Matched data-scaling splits (lingala_1hr/5hr/10hr/20hr) used for low-resource ASR ablations; useful as standard benchmarks.

name: Rasheed Mudasiru multi-speaker conversational audio - SLR162
notes: 63 minutes of overlapping multi-party conversational English with background noise, released for audio forensics / speaker separation / speech enhancement. OpenSLR lists the language only as 'English'; the Nigerian provenance is inferred from the author and is NOT confirmed.

name: SautiDB: Nigerian Accent Dataset Collection
notes: 919 post-processed clips (~59 min) of Nigerian-accented English crowdsourced via a web app for accent-transfer research; very small but openly downloadable.

name: mounkaila144/zarma-collecte-privee
notes: 41 WAV files of field-collected Zarma; essentially a seed set, no card.

name: Mozilla Common Voice - Tigrinya
notes: Essentially empty: CV 26.0 had only 75 validated clips (~6.5 minutes) from 16 speakers; the Tigrinya locale needs community mobilisation.

name: Dogon Dogul Dom audio files (Dogon Languages Project, U. Michigan Deep Blue)
notes: ~14 minutes of narrative Dogul Dom with PDF transcriptions and translations; part of a larger Deep Blue deposit of Dogon-language field recordings — the only openly licensed Dogon audio found.

name: Speech-data/Lingala-Speech-Dataset
notes: Single 46-second female recording - effectively a demo sample, listed for completeness only.

name: 1rsh/speech-qa-bhojpuri-hi-karya
notes: ADJACENT (Indian Bhojpuri): Karya-collected spoken question-answering audio in Bhojpuri/Hindi; multi-purpose but usable as ASR material for Bhojpuri transfer.

name: 2M-Belebele (facebook/2M-Belebele)
notes: Speech recordings of the Belebele reading-comprehension passages in 74 spoken languages including kea_Latn; built for spoken QA but directly reusable as read-speech ASR/TTS data.

name: abdouaziz/pulaar_speech_2
notes: Small community Pulaar speech dump from a Senegalese NLP developer; undocumented, verify content before use.

name: Accent Classification Dataset (Ghana)
notes: Ghanaian-accent labelled speech built for accent classification; repurposable for accented-English ASR evaluation.

name: addisai/amharic-tts-benchmark
notes: Evaluation set for Amharic speech synthesis from Addis AI; small benchmark rather than training data.

name: ADI17_filtered_LIB (Libyan Arabic subset of ADI17)
notes: 34.1k audio segments (2.9-30 s) filtered as Libyan from ADI17, with train/dev/test splits; dialect-ID labels rather than verified transcripts, so treat as weakly labelled - still the largest single pool of Libyan Arabic audio on the Hub.

name: AdwumaTech African language speech data services
notes: Ghana-oriented vendor offering native-speaker speech/NLP data collection and annotation for African languages; bespoke, no catalogue hours.

name: African Speech Technology Afrikaans-Afrikaans Speech Corpus
notes: L1 (white) Afrikaans telephone speech. From the 2000-2004 African Speech Technology project (fixed + mobile telephone, orthographic and phonetic transcription).

name: African Speech Technology Black-Afrikaans Speech Corpus
notes: Afrikaans as spoken by L1 speakers of indigenous languages. From the 2000-2004 African Speech Technology project (fixed + mobile telephone, orthographic and phonetic transcription).

name: African Speech Technology Black-English Speech Corpus
languages: South African English (Black South African English)
notes: English spoken by isiXhosa/isiZulu/Sesotho L1 speakers - the canonical Black South African English speech corpus. From the 2000-2004 African Speech Technology project (fixed + mobile telephone, orthographic and phonetic transcription).

name: African Speech Technology Coloured-Afrikaans Speech Corpus
notes: Cape Flats / Coloured Afrikaans variety - one of very few corpora of this sociolect. From the 2000-2004 African Speech Technology project (fixed + mobile telephone, orthographic and phonetic transcription).

name: African Speech Technology Coloured-English Speech Corpus
notes: Cape Flats English variety telephone speech. From the 2000-2004 African Speech Technology project (fixed + mobile telephone, orthographic and phonetic transcription).

name: African Speech Technology isiZulu Speech Corpus
notes: isiZulu telephone speech from the AST project. From the 2000-2004 African Speech Technology project (fixed + mobile telephone, orthographic and phonetic transcription).

name: African Speech Technology Sesotho Speech Corpus
notes: Sesotho telephone speech from the AST project. From the 2000-2004 African Speech Technology project (fixed + mobile telephone, orthographic and phonetic transcription).

name: AfricaNLP crowd-sourced digits keyword-spotting corpus (crowd-speech-africa)
notes: 808 MB / 1k-10k clips of crowd-collected spoken digits and keywords in African languages from the AfricaNLP 'afro-speech' effort (Chris Emezue et al.). Gated behind an agreement not to re-identify speakers; dataset card is empty so languages, hours and licence are unverified. Useful for keyword spotting, not general ASR.
language_note: This source describes its coverage in prose rather than naming individual languages, so it carries no ISO 639-3 codes. The source's own wording is kept in `languages`.

name: Afrikaans multi-speaker TTS corpus
notes: Low-cost multi-voice TTS recordings by non-professional volunteers (MuST, NWU); SADiLaR-hosted sibling of the OpenSLR-32 release.

name: AFRILANG (mimba/afrilang)
notes: Forced-aligned (Aeneas) New Testament audio segments <30s built for Whisper/MMS fine-tuning; Ngiemboon (Bamileke) live, Adamawa Fulfulde and Bulu announced as in progress.

name: AfriSpeak Kinyarwanda female TTS dataset
notes: Voice-actor Kinyarwanda TTS corpus with train/dev/test manifests; dataset viewer currently broken by inconsistent column casing. A male counterpart exists at .../afrispeak_kinyarwanda_male_tts_dataset.

name: AfriSpeech african-speech-public_v1
languages: 142 subsets incl. Mauritian Creole, Seychellois Creole, Malagasy, Lingala, Kirundi
notes: Aggregated public African speech with ISO 639-3 labels; notable because it is one of the very few places with any Mauritian Creole and Seychellois Creole audio. Licence not stated on the card - verify before use.

name: AfriSpeech/open-bible-speech-african
notes: Verse-aligned Open.Bible audio for 19 African languages including Lingala, with book/chapter/verse and speaker metadata.

name: AfriVoice Kikongo (MANIANGA)
notes: AfriVoice-derived Kikongo ASR set; Kikongo is also a major northern-Angola language, so this is the closest usable speech data for Angolan Kikongo/Fiote, though speakers are likely Congolese.

name: Afrivoice Swahili ASR (domain splits)
notes: Re-packaged Afrivoice Swahili with agriculture/education/financial/government/health configs and instruction-format prompts; ~120k train rows per domain.

name: ai4bharat/Rural_Women_Bhojpuri
notes: ADJACENT (Uttar Pradesh Bhojpuri): 78,800 rows (400 real + 78,000 synthetic train, 444 benchmark) from rural women across age and occupation strata, with Bhojpuri and Hindi-script transcripts.

name: ALFFA Hausa ASR corpus
notes: ALFFA released open Kaldi recipes for Hausa but the audio itself must be purchased from ELDA/ELRA — the repo states 'YOU NEED TO BUY THE RESOURCES AT ELDA'. Amharic, Swahili and Wolof audio are free; Hausa is not.

name: ALFFA Swahili News (HF repackaging)
notes: HuggingFace-ready packaging of the ALFFA Swahili broadcast-news material; convenient loader for the OpenSLR data.

name: Alioukun/kallaama-pulaar-denoised (and -filtered)
notes: Cleaned/denoised derivative of the Kallaama Pulaar split — useful preprocessing already done, same CC-BY licence chain.

name: Alwaly/Wolof_TTS
notes: 40k row Wolof TTS set (36k train / 4k test) with male and female speakers; appears to overlap heavily with galsenai/wolof_tts.

name: Appen off-the-shelf speech & audio datasets
notes: VENDOR: read, conversational and call-centre speech across 80+ languages and 80+ countries; the public catalogue does not name Shona, Ndebele, Chichewa, Bemba or African Portuguese, so coverage must be confirmed with sales.

name: arabic-dialect-identification (ADI baseline + data recipes)
notes: Reference recipes, segment lists and pretrained models for ADI17 country-level dialect ID over all 17 Arabic countries; the practical entry point for reconstructing the North African portions of ADI17.

name: arabic-egy-cleaned
notes: 104k cleaned 0.5-10 s clips with Egyptian Arabic transcripts, merged from egyptian-arabic-lines, an Egyptian YouTube collection and egyptian-arabic-wavs; provenance/licence of the constituent parts is not documented, so audit before commercial use.

name: asr-africa/ASR_Evaluation_dataset
notes: Shared held-out evaluation suite of the ASR-Africa project; Lingala is one of the tagged languages, so it doubles as a Lingala test set.

name: ASR-ALFFA (MagicHub mirror)
notes: Sign-in-required mirror of ALFFA; same Amharic content as OpenSLR 25, useful as an alternative download path.

name: Automatic Speech Recognition in Wolof (Kaggle, kingabzpro)
notes: Kaggle packaging of the AI4D/Zindi Wolof public-transport ASR challenge data; small but a clean labelled starter set.

name: b1n1yam/afaan-oromo-tts
notes: Afan Oromo TTS set published alongside Addis AI's open-source Shook speech models; companion set b1n1yam/waxal-orm-tts-merged merges the WAXAL Oromo TTS data.

name: badrex/malagasy-speech-full
notes: Largest openly downloadable Malagasy ASR set on the Hub: 31,635 audio+text rows (train 25.8k / val 2.81k / test 3.02k), 124 GB parquet; dataset card is empty so provenance and licence are undocumented.

name: BATBAINA/fulfulde-dataset-asr-agri
notes: 1,389 short (0.9-3.4 s) Fulfulde utterances of agricultural vocabulary with gender labels; gender-balanced but very small and word-level.

name: BBC News Pidgin audio/video archive
notes: Daily West African Pidgin news with audio/video bulletins and matching written articles since 2017 - the largest single reservoir of transcribable Pidgin broadcast speech; BBC terms restrict redistribution.

name: BBC World Service Somali / Amharic / Afaan Oromo / Tigrinya
notes: RAW SOURCE: BBC's four Horn-language services publish daily radio bulletins and video alongside written text (bbc.com/somali, /amharic, /afaanoromoo, /tigrinya). Highest-quality studio audio in the region, but BBC terms restrict reuse and the sites block automated fetching.

name: bemba-collection
notes: Aggregation of publicly available Bemba speech sources; contents unverified, treat as a convenience bundle of BembaSpeech/BIG-C derivatives.

name: bemba-speech-csikasote (HF mirror)
notes: Third-party HuggingFace mirror of BembaSpeech; useful if the GitHub release is unavailable.

name: BEMBA_big_c (HuggingFace mirror of BIG-C)
notes: Loader-ready BIG-C repackaging used by the ASR-Africa / Makerere benchmarking work; convenient for fine-tuning pipelines.

name: BembaSpeech (CovianHive mirror)
notes: Another HF mirror of BembaSpeech; metadata not curated, verify splits before use.

name: bembaspeech_plus_jw_processed
notes: BembaSpeech augmented with JW.org Bemba audio by the original author; shows the JW religious-audio harvest route in practice, licence of the JW portion unclear.

name: benjaminogbonna/nigerian_common_voice_dataset
notes: Community re-packaging of the Nigerian-language slices of Common Voice for easier Whisper fine-tuning; derivative, not new audio.

name: Benji-fish/ethiopian-languages-speech-dataset
notes: 1,480 long-form clips (12-59s) with dialect labels (e.g. Amharic Shewa and Wollo) and speaker gender; small but rare for dialect-annotated Ethiopian speech.

name: bible.is / Faith Comes By Hearing audio New Testaments
notes: Underlying source for CMU Wilderness, MMS and DONDO: chapter-level studio readings with parallel text. Streaming only, redistribution not permitted, but 11-20 h per language can be force-aligned. Confirmed present for the nine codes listed.

name: birma091/zarma-tts-dataset
notes: 332 Zarma audio/text pairs (2-15 s), text appears to be scripture; tiny but one of only two Zarma speech sets on HuggingFace.

name: BSG DataWorks Nigerian speech collections
notes: Nigeria-based vendor: Nigerian-accented English and Yoruba available for evaluation, Igbo/Hausa/Pidgin in collection, Kanuri/Efik and other minority languages on commission. No published hours; quotes in 48 h across sub-$5k to $50k+ tiers.

name: Casablanca
notes: Multi-dialectal Arabic ASR benchmark over 8 dialects (Algerian, Egyptian, Emirati, Jordanian, Mauritanian, Moroccan, Palestinian, Yemeni) with transcription, gender, dialect and code-switch labels; the only public benchmark with a Mauritanian Hassaniya split. Public Hub release is dev+test only (~844/843 rows).

name: Casual South African accented English speech sample
notes: Vendor sample of casual SA-accented English on HuggingFace; small teaser for a larger paid collection, details unverified.

name: chichewa-transcipt-dataset
notes: Transcript companion to the above Chichewa audio repo; unverified, listed as a lead for Malawian grassroots data.

name: chichewa-trigrams-speech-text-parallel
notes: Large set of short trigram-level speech/text pairs for Chichewa; unclear whether audio is human or TTS-generated, so useful mainly for pronunciation/lexicon work.

name: chichewa_audio_trans
notes: Community-uploaded Chichewa audio-with-transcription repo from a Malawian contributor; size and licence unverified, one of a small cluster of Rhode01 Chichewa repos.

name: chichewa_english_code_switch_dataset
notes: Chichewa-English code-switching dataset; likely text-only (a sibling repo by another user was empty), but the only Chichewa-English code-switch resource located.

name: chichewa_voice_agent
notes: Voice-agent oriented Chichewa dataset; unverified contents, included as a Malawian speech-application lead.

name: COCOON / Pangloss Fang collection (CNRS)
notes: CNRS language-documentation archive with field recordings of Fang (Equatorial Guinea/Gabon); transcribed narratives, mostly Creative Commons or restricted per deposit - needs manual inspection.

name: Commercial African speech data vendors (bespoke collection)
notes: Vendors that sell or collect African speech to order: Appen (built the IARPA Babel Swahili, Zulu and Igbo packs - the strongest verified African speech-collection track record of any vendor), Way With Words (South Africa based, African language transcription and collection), Digital Umuganda (Rwanda; also publishes openly - see its Afrivoice entries), Shaip, Datatang, Magic Data, Sigma AI, TransPerfect DataForce, Summa Linguae, Innodata, CloudFactory (Kenya delivery centres) and Uhura/Volara. Only Appen's and Digital Umuganda's African speech output is independently verifiable; for the others no public African speech SKU could be confirmed and no URL is asserted here.
language_note: This source describes its coverage in prose rather than naming individual languages, so it carries no ISO 639-3 codes. The source's own wording is kept in `languages`.

name: Common Voice Kinyarwanda-English aligned set (Mbaza NLP)
notes: Kinyarwanda CV audio paired with English translations; usable for speech translation as well as ASR.

name: Common Voice Scripted Speech (Hausa, Dioula)
notes: Common Voice 26.0 has a modest Hausa set (~255 MB) and a very small Dioula set (~10 MB); no Wolof, Fula, Bambara, Mooré, Zarma, Kanuri or Soninke. Datasets moved from HuggingFace to Mozilla Data Collective in Oct 2025.

name: Common Voice Swahili (small, CDLI subset)
notes: Small curated Common Voice Swahili subset published by UCL's Centre for Digital Language Inclusion as a typical-speech control set against their nonstandard-speech corpora.

name: CommonVoice22-Sidon (restored audio, incl. Basaa)
notes: Common Voice 22 passed through Sidon speech restoration and upsampled to 48kHz - makes the noisy Basaa crowd recordings usable for TTS.

name: Congo-digital-service/audios-lingala-annotatees
languages_clean: French (Congo, The Democratic Republic of the)
notes: First version of the annotated Lingala rural-radio set; superseded by v2 but may contain different segments.

name: Congo-digital-service/audios-lingala-annotatees-v2
languages_clean: French (Congo, The Democratic Republic of the)
notes: 18.8k annotated segments from rural-radio programmes and cooperative interviews, explicitly labelled Lingala vs Français-Lingala code-switch.

name: Congolese Wav2Vec datasets experiment (code + data pointers)
notes: Collection/preprocessing scripts and radio-URL lists used to build LRSC and CSRC; the practical route to regenerating the raw audio.

name: Coptic Language Text-to-Speech Seed dataset
notes: Small hobbyist seed corpus of recorded Coptic sentences for TTS - essentially the only speech dataset for Coptic; liturgical chant recordings on church sites are the other (unlabelled) option.

name: crowd-oshiwambo-speech-greetings
notes: Tiny crowdsourced set (<1k clips) of Oshiwambo greetings - as far as this survey could establish, the ONLY purpose-built open Oshiwambo speech dataset.

name: Crowdsourced Corpus for Moroccan Darija Speech-to-Text
notes: Crowdsourced Darija speech-to-text corpus described in IJETT 2024; paper documents collection protocol, data release not confirmed.

name: Crowdsourced high-quality Nigerian English speech data set - SLR70
notes: Google crowdsourced Nigerian English read speech recorded in Lagos and London, split by speaker gender, manually QC'd. The only open studio-quality Nigerian English TTS corpus in the Google OpenSLR series.

name: Crowdsourced high-quality Yoruba speech data set - SLR86
notes: Google/Gutkin et al. (Interspeech 2020) crowdsourced Yoruba read speech, separate female and male sets. Together with SLR32 and SLR70 this is the whole African footprint of Google's 'high quality TTS data for X' OpenSLR series - there is no Swahili, Hausa or Amharic entry in that series.

name: Curated Crowdsourced Luganda and Swahili Speech for TTS
notes: Common Voice audio filtered down to six female speakers per language for end-to-end TTS training; paper in Data in Brief (ScienceDirect S2352340925006390).

name: Dawa Voice Kirundi-French
notes: Jitimay (Burundian) Kirundi-French voice dataset; small and undocumented, and the sibling repo Jitimay/Audio_in_Kirundi is currently empty - Burundi is effectively a data desert.

name: Defined.ai speech data marketplace
notes: Marketplace advertises global coverage but the public dataset listing surfaces no African language or African-accented English product; Arabic is the only Africa-adjacent language visible. Bespoke collection is the realistic route. Unverified African catalogue.

name: Dendi of Parakou multi-speaker speech dataset
notes: 676 quiet-room sentence recordings by one male and one female Dendi speaker from Parakou; tiny but the only Dendi speech data found, and CC-BY-4.0.

name: Development of Hausa dataset: a baseline for speech recognition
notes: Data in Brief paper releasing a Hausa read-speech baseline corpus (Nile University of Nigeria); hours not stated in accessible metadata.

name: Digital Umuganda Kinyarwanda Common Voice working set
notes: Digital Umuganda's curation/cleaning pipeline and splits over Kinyarwanda Common Voice; the organisation that drove the 2,000+ hr CV Kinyarwanda collection.

name: Digital Umuganda other speech releases (Afrivoice_Kinyarwanda, Afrivoice_legacy, ASR Fellowship Challenge)
notes: 22 datasets in total on the org page, including Afrivoice_Kinyarwanda, Afrivoice_legacy, a common-voice Kinyarwanda text set, anv_test_data_nt_swahili and a 190k-row ASR Fellowship Challenge set. Individual hour counts for these were not verified. Digital Umuganda is also the leading commercial African speech-data vendor (Kinyarwanda ASR/TTS for government).

name: DigitalUmuganda_AfriVoice_shona
notes: Loader-ready Shona split of AfriVoice: 16,800 transcribed clips from 125 speakers with gender metadata; the practical entry point for Shona ASR fine-tuning.

name: DONDO w2v-BERT base models (Sierra Leone family: Krio/Mende/Temne)
notes: w2v-bert-kri-men-tem-en multilingual ASR base model released by KhayaAI; states training audio is 'predominantly read speech derived from religious texts' but gives no hours and does not release the corpus.

name: DoReCo Beja corpus
notes: Martine Vanhove's Beja narratives (fieldwork 2003-2011), phone-level time-aligned in DoReCo (DOI 10.34847/nkl.edd011t1); the best phonetically aligned audio resource for Beja, small and non-commercial.

name: DVoice (Dialectal Voice) - Darija
notes: Crowdsourced open Darija ASR dataset from AIOX Labs (2,392 train / 600 test utterances in v1); paired SpeechBrain wav2vec2 recipes published as speechbrain/asr-wav2vec2-dvoice-darija. Small, read-style, and hour count not documented.

name: DVoice / ALFFA Fongbe
notes: SpeechBrain's DVoice Fongbe recipe trains on an ALFFA_PUBLIC Fongbe partition (9.19% WER); the model card is the only public pointer to that audio, which is not in the free ALFFA distribution.

name: DVoice Darija
notes: 11,348 Darija clips with transcriptions, extended from Common Voice-style crowdsourcing; CC0 so unrestricted. Includes augmented variants, so deduplicate before training.

name: DVoice Wolof (AIOX Labs / speechbrain DVoice collection)
notes: DVoice is a multi-African-language crowdsourced corpus (Darija, Wolof, Swahili, Fongbe, Amharic); only the trained Wolof model card is public, the audio needs a request to the DVoice team.

name: edacc_accents (HuggingFace mirror)
notes: Community re-upload of EdAcc with accent labels; convenient for filtering African-accented subsets.

name: ELAR: Linguistic Documentation of Siwi Berber (Siwa Oasis)
notes: Field documentation collection (Valentina Schiattarella) of Siwi, the only Berber language of Egypt; narratives and conversation with ELAN annotation - the principal audio resource for Siwi, access-controlled.

name: ELBC / Liberia Broadcasting System news archive
