notes: State broadcaster ELBC's news site, identified as LBS's official outlet; primary harvestable source of Liberian English / Liberian Kreyol broadcast speech. Volume of posted audio not verified.

name: Emakhuwa-Monolingual (LIACC)
notes: TEXT ONLY: Felermino Ali / LIACC monolingual Emakhuwa corpus. Essential for ASR language modelling and TTS text normalisation; confirms the Emakhuwa programme is text/MT-first with no released speech corpus.

name: Emakhuwa-Portuguese-News-MT (LIACC)
notes: TEXT ONLY: Emakhuwa-Portuguese parallel news corpus (EMNLP 2024). Listed because it is the anchor resource for any future Emakhuwa speech-translation work.

name: Endangered Languages Archive (ELAR) - Khoisan collections (N|uu, Khoekhoegowab, Ju|'hoansi, Naro)
notes: RAW SOURCE: field documentation deposits (elicitation, narrative, conversation) with ELAN transcriptions for Khoisan languages; N|uu has only a handful of remaining speakers, so these archives are the entire available record. Many files are access-restricted and must be requested.

name: English-Juba Arabic parallel resources (for prompt/text pairing)
notes: Text-only English-Juba Arabic parallel data; listed because it is the realistic prompt source for any future Juba Arabic read-speech collection (no audio).

name: Ephrem/Amharic_ASR_Dataset
notes: Small community Amharic ASR upload with no dataset card; verify content before use.

name: Eritrean Ministry of Information / Eri-TV & Dimtsi Hafash
notes: RAW SOURCE and effectively the ONLY source of audio for Eritrea's minority languages (Saho, Bilen, Kunama, Nara): state radio Dimtsi Hafash broadcasts in all nine national languages, with Eri-TV video on the EriTVEritreaOfficial YouTube channel. Web portal itself is Tigrinya/Arabic/English only; no transcripts.

name: EthioNLP resources (negative result for speech)
notes: NEGATIVE RESULT: EthioNLP (EthioLLM, EthioPOS, EthioSenti, EthioHate, Amharic-LLaMA) and the related HornMT/HornNLP and Lesan AI efforts are text and machine-translation only - no speech or audio releases. Their text is still useful as ASR language-model data.

name: Ethiopian Broadcasting Corporation (EBC) archive
notes: RAW SOURCE: national broadcaster with explicit audio and video sections plus live streams in Amharic, Afan Oromo, English and Arabic; the English channel is a route to Ethiopian-accented English.

name: evanmazor/aisha-krio-dataset
notes: 1,360 clips (1,160 train / 205 test) of Krio voice commands from 17 participants, built for a voice-assistant ('Aisha'); command-domain only.

name: evanmazor/aisha-krio-dataset-phase-1-and-2
notes: Combined phase-1+2 release of the Aisha Krio command corpus; larger than the base set but undocumented.

name: evie-8/afrivoices-v2
notes: Working re-release of AfriVoice image-description speech including the Lingala partition; useful as a cleaned alternative.

name: Eyaa-Tom
notes: 20 k+ parallel audio-text segments across 10 Togolese languages with French/English translations (religious core plus health, finance and public-service domains); the public HF slice is only ~1,010 rows, so most of the corpus is not yet released. The only resource found for Kabiye, Tem, Aja, Moba, Lama, Konkomba, Bassar and Nawdm.

name: facebook/mms-tts-mlg
notes: VITS Malagasy TTS checkpoint (36.3M params) from MMS; the only off-the-shelf Malagasy synthesiser, usable to bootstrap synthetic training data (ONNX ports exist).

name: Faith Comes By Hearing / Bible Brain (Digital Bible Platform) audio Bibles
notes: Dramatised and non-dramatised audio New/Old Testaments in over a thousand languages, with a developer API (Bible Brain / Digital Bible Platform) that returns audio plus verse timing - i.e. near-aligned ASR/TTS data. Terms require an API key and are not open-licence; exact African language count not verified here. The main alternative supply line to MMS-style scripture corpora.

name: Fana Media Corporation multilingual broadcast archive
notes: RAW SOURCE and the most linguistically diverse Ethiopian broadcaster: news and Fana TV output in seven languages including Afar and Somali, both of which have almost no open data.

name: Farmerline ML African language audio sets (Kikuyu, Kamba, Kinyarwanda, Luganda, Somali)
notes: Gated audio+text datasets (~1.7 GB each) from Farmerline's Darli/voice work; siblings exist at FarmerlineML/kamba_dataset, /kinyarwanda_dataset, /luganda_dataset_2.0, /somali_cleaned_dataset. Licence and hours undisclosed - the only Kamba speech beyond FLEURS.

name: FarmerlineML akan_dataset / akan_dataset_ALL
notes: Farmerline's in-house Akan ASR training data (a twi_dataset_2.0 and Twi_TTS2026_dataset also exist in the same org); gated behind contact sharing.

name: FarmerlineML fongbe_dataset
notes: 786 MB of Fongbe audio+text (10 k-100 k rows) held by Farmerline; gated, card undocumented.

name: FarmerlineML tts_hausa_dataset
notes: Farmerline Hausa TTS corpus (a newer TTS_hausa_new also exists); gated, size/licence not documented on the card.

name: FarmerlineML/2026_krio_TTS
notes: 537 Krio audio/transcript pairs (1-16 s) of product/customer-service utterances, from Farmerline (Ghana); small but clean and paired with released Krio TTS checkpoints.

name: FarmerlineML/krio_dataset_2
notes: 2.42 GB gated Krio audio+text set, 1K-10K rows; empty README, access requires contact-info sharing.

name: FarmerlineML/wolof_dataset
notes: 1.94 GB gated Wolof audio/text set from Farmerline (Ghanaian agri-tech); conditions must be accepted, no card metadata published.

name: Faso Speech — Dioula digits (madoss/faso-speech-dioula-digits)
notes: 1,698 spoken-digit clips (numbers 1-4) collected in Burkina Faso for keyword spotting; derived from Zenodo record 8320370 (Université de Bordeaux / ESI).

name: flagship-ai/cameroon_bibles
notes: ~496k-item companion text corpus of Cameroonian Bible translations; the alignment target for spoken-Bible ASR/TTS work on Cameroonian languages.

name: FLEURS Kinyarwanda (mbazaNLP packaging)
notes: Kinyarwanda FLEURS split repackaged by Mbaza NLP for benchmarking Rwandan ASR models.

name: fleurysraj/malagasy-speech-full-bucket
notes: Apparent re-bucketed derivative of badrex/malagasy-speech-full; listed on the Hub but undocumented - treat as a duplicate rather than new audio.

name: FLORES-200
notes: Text, not speech - but it is the source text for FLEURS/FLEURS-R and therefore defines which languages get n-way parallel speech evaluation. 3,001 sentences from 842 web articles, 200 languages. Exact African count not verified here; it includes the Arabic varieties and most NLLB African languages.
language_note: This source describes its coverage in prose rather than naming individual languages, so it carries no ISO 639-3 codes. The source's own wording is kept in `languages`.

name: FongbeSpeechDataset
notes: Fongbe speech data collection and training code from the Google NLP Hack Series (2nd place); audio itself is downloaded separately from Zenodo. CC0 licence is unusually permissive for Fon.

name: Forensic Algerian Corpus (Algerian speaker-comparison corpus)
notes: Purpose-built Algerian corpus for forensic speaker comparison (read + spontaneous + telephone-degraded conditions); designed for speaker ID but usable for Algerian ASR/adaptation - access via the authors.

name: FrancophonIA/Francais-Shimaore
notes: TEXT-ONLY French-Shimaore lexical resource; included because Mayotte's languages have essentially no speech data and this is usable lexicon/text for a Shimaore TTS front-end.

name: FrancophonIA/Petit_lexique_Creole_reunionais-francais
notes: TEXT-ONLY small Reunion-Creole-French lexicon; no audio, but the only structured rcf resource on the Hub besides hugohow/creole_reunion.

name: GALE Phase 4 Arabic Broadcast News Speech (LDC2018S05)
notes: One of the many GALE Arabic broadcast releases (news and conversation, Phases 1-4) recorded off pan-Arab and North African channels; licensed per-corpus through LDC membership or purchase.

name: galsenai/wolof_tts
notes: 40k audio/text pairs with gender labels, packaged by GalsenAI (largely the Zenodo Wolof TTS data); used for the xTTS-v2-wolof voice.

name: Gamayun language data kits
notes: CLEAR Global/TWB parallel text kits plus recorded audio for humanitarian languages including Swahili variants; source of the Kenyan-Swahili-Speech set.

name: Ge'ez liturgical chant audio (no dataset)
notes: NEGATIVE RESULT: all seven HuggingFace datasets tagged gez are text-only (wiktionary, panlex, biblenlp, abyssinica-synth OCR). No Ge'ez speech corpus and no MMS voice exists; Ethiopian and Eritrean Orthodox liturgical recordings on YouTube are the only route.

name: Ghanaian English mistranscription corrections corpus
notes: 380,377 rows of ASR error/correction pairs harvested from Ghanaian news YouTube - text, not audio, but directly targets Ghanaian-English ASR adaptation and points at the underlying scrapeable YouTube audio.

name: GhanaNLP ghana-asr-audio (UNICEF speech)
notes: 4,450 half-hour chunks of UNICEF Ghana health/education audio; paired transcripts live in the companion ghana-asr-transcripts repo.

name: GhanaNLP ghana-speech (Bible speech, 42 Ghanaian languages)
notes: 1-10 M aligned Bible-audio rows across 42 languages of Ghana (Akuapem Twi subset alone is 52.7 k rows) — the widest single source for Ghana's smaller languages, including Hausa as spoken in Ghana.

name: GhanaNLP navigation-corpus-dagbani-speech
notes: 52.8 k short (1-5 s) Dagbani utterances naming Ghanaian shops, landmarks and institutions — built for navigation/voice-assistant use; Twi and Ewe navigation-speech siblings exist in the same org.

name: GhanaNLP twi-female-speech-tts
notes: 1,470 single-female-speaker ('Akosua') Twi recordings with transcripts; the voice behind GhanaNLP's Khaya TTS.

name: GhanaNLP twi-speech-text-multispeaker-16k
notes: 15,600 short multi-speaker Twi clips (0.04-10 s) at 16 kHz with transcripts; the main community Twi ASR set behind the Khaya stack.

name: ghanaopenai/ghana-female-speech
notes: Female-voice studio news audio in nine Ghanaian languages (~5-7 k rows each) with confidence scores; the only speech data found for Nzema, Ahanta and Sehwi.

name: Global Recordings Network (GRN) audio library
languages: many minority languages incl. Balanta, Bissa, Bomu, Dogon varieties, Jola, Soninke, Kissi
notes: RAW SOURCE: free recordings in 6,577 language varieties, browsable by country — the only audio at all for many Sahel minority languages (Bissa, Bomu, individual Dogon varieties, Balanta). Scripts are known per programme so semi-supervised alignment is feasible; licence needs clearing.
language_note: This source describes its coverage in prose rather than naming individual languages, so it carries no ISO 639-3 codes. The source's own wording is kept in `languages`.

name: Global Recordings Network - Asante Twi
notes: Asante Twi narrated audio archive with scripts.

name: Global Recordings Network - Basaa
notes: Downloadable MP3 Bible-teaching and 'Words of Life' programmes in Basaa; GRN has comparable pages for most Cameroonian, Chadian, CAR, Gabonese and Congolese languages, making it the broadest raw audio source for this cluster.

name: Global Recordings Network - Egypt audio archive
notes: Free MP3 gospel/story recordings in Egyptian Arabic, Cairene, Sa'idi and Eastern Egyptian Bedawi - one of the only audio sources at all for Sa'idi and Bedawi Arabic; scripts exist but are not distributed as aligned transcripts, so alignment work is needed.

name: Global Recordings Network - Ewe (Togo)
notes: Togo-recorded Ewe programmes; useful for Togolese Ewe accent coverage distinct from the Ghanaian BibleTTS speaker.

name: Global Recordings Network - Fon
notes: Fon audio programmes with accompanying scripts; one of very few additional Fon audio sources beyond FFSTC.

name: Global Recordings Network - Kabyle audio
notes: Free downloadable MP3 story/teaching sets and songs in Kabyle; scripts are published separately in some cases, so partial transcript recovery is possible. Parallel GRN pages exist for Tachelhit, Tarifit, Chaoui, Tamasheq and Hassaniya.

name: Global Recordings Network - Nigeria language archive
notes: GRN states 500 languages/dialects recorded in Nigeria — narrated evangelistic scripts, mostly with matching printed text. Easily the widest coverage of Nigerian minority languages (Tiv, Idoma, Nupe, Izon, Berom, Gbagyi, Urhobo) but needs scraping, alignment and licence clearance.

name: Global Recordings Network - Yoruba
notes: Yoruba narrated programme archive with script text; usable as forced-alignment fodder.

name: Global Recordings Network audio archive
notes: RAW SOURCE: short gospel//story recordings in hundreds of Southern African language varieties including San languages and Khoekhoegowab; often the ONLY recorded audio for these varieties, but scripts are not always published so transcripts must be reconstructed. (Site returned 403 to automated fetching during this survey.)

name: Global Recordings Network — Cape Verde language archive
notes: Separate Kabuverdianu and Kabuverdianu-Barlavento recording sets — the only source found that explicitly distinguishes the Barlavento variant in audio.

name: Global Recordings Network — Dioula recordings
notes: ~10 programme sets downloadable as MP3 (294 MB full quality, 90 MB low-bitrate); GRN has comparable per-language pages for most Ivorian and Liberian languages, reachable by ISO code.

name: Global Recordings Network — Sierra Leone language archive
notes: 16 Sierra Leonean languages with downloadable MP3 programme sets (Look Listen & Live, Words of Life); scripts exist per programme so audio can be semi-aligned. Covers several languages with zero other data (Sherbro, Krim, Loko, Kuranko).

name: goaicorp/goai-dioula-speech
notes: 4.93 GB gated Dioula (Jula) speech/text set from the Burkinabè GO AI Corporation; undocumented card, contact-info gate. A cleaned variant exists as goaicorp/new-dioula-speech-clean.

name: goaicorp/new-dioula-speech-clean
notes: ~10,929 cleaned 48 kHz WAV examples pairing Dioula utterances with French translations; usable for ASR, TTS and speech translation.

name: Google Project Relate
notes: Negative/limited result: Project Relate is an Android app for non-standard speech built from over a million recorded samples, but no dataset is released and the page states no language or region coverage; sign-ups are closed. Not a usable African data source - included because it is often cited as one.

name: GRN - Bushi / Kibushi (no recordings)
notes: Negative result: GRN explicitly has no recordings in Bushi/Kibushi (~69,000 speakers in Mayotte); no speech data of any kind was located for this language.

name: GRN audio recordings - Malagasy, Merina
notes: Raw source: 'Look, Listen & Live' (8 books), four 'Words of Life' collections and 40-section 'Good News' in Merina Malagasy, bulk-downloadable as MP3 with matching scripts - alignable into read-speech ASR/TTS data.

name: GRN audio recordings - Morisyen (Mauritian Creole)
notes: Raw source: 'Good News' (40 sections) and 'Words of Life' in Kreol Morisien, 47.1 MB MP3 bundle with published scripts - effectively the only openly downloadable Mauritian Creole speech audio found.

name: GRN audio recordings - Reunion French Creole
notes: Raw source: 'Words of Life' in Kreol Reunione, 55.6 MB MP3 bundle with scripts; the only downloadable Reunion Creole speech audio found (~555k speakers otherwise undocumented for ASR).

name: GRN audio recordings - Seychelles French Creole (none available)
notes: Negative result recorded for completeness: GRN states it has no recordings in Seselwa; only the Jesus Film dub is linked, so the usual religious-audio route is nearly empty for Seychelles.

name: GRN audio recordings - Shimaore (Mayotte Comorian)
notes: Raw source and the richest GRN bundle in the cluster: 'Good News' plus the full 8-book 'Look, Listen & Live' series in Shimaore, 395.7 MB MP3 (103.9 MB low-bitrate) with scripts.

name: GRN audio recordings - Shimwali (Moheli Comorian)
notes: Raw source: 'The Two Roads' and 'Good News' in Shimwali, 49.6 MB MP3 bundle; smallest-population Comorian variety and the only audio found for it.

name: GRN audio recordings - Shindzwani (Anjouan Comorian)
notes: Raw source: 40-section 'Good News' in Shindzwani, 45.2 MB MP3 bundle (12.9 MB low-bitrate) with scripts; the only Shindzwani-specific audio located.

name: Hausa Speech Corpus (Mendeley Data)
notes: Mendeley-hosted Hausa speech corpus; landing page blocked automated access so size/licence unverified.

name: Hausa Speech Dataset (Mendeley Data)
notes: Second, separate Mendeley Hausa speech deposit; details unverified.

name: High quality TTS data for four South African languages - SLR32
notes: Google + North-West University multi-speaker studio TTS data; the first entry in Google's 'high quality TTS data for X' OpenSLR series and still the standard open South African TTS baseline.

name: HobyTahiry/malagasy-speech-full_hoby
notes: Another Hub copy/variant of the malagasy-speech-full collection (a further copy exists at rorandri/malagasy-speech-full_hoby_copy); no independent audio.

name: hramphul/Kreol-Morisien
notes: TEXT-ONLY (no audio): monolingual/parallel Kreol Morisien corpus from a Mauritian researcher; useful as TTS text and ASR language-model data given the total absence of Kreol speech corpora.

name: ICE spoken components (East Africa, Ghana, South Africa)
notes: ICE-East Africa (Kenya/Tanzania), ICE-Ghana and the South African component are distributed primarily as orthographic transcripts; audio is generally NOT released (ICE-Nigeria is the exception). Log as raw/negative: valuable transcript text for LM adaptation, not usable audio.

name: ICE-Nigeria (International Corpus of English, Nigerian component)
notes: Unusually, this ICE component publishes the actual sound recordings for the spoken part (conversations, broadcast news, lectures, phone calls) - 16 zip archives, 19.7 GB, with ELAN .eaf time-aligned transcriptions. The single richest free Nigerian English speech archive; licence terms need checking with ice-corpora.net.

name: IDEA International Dialects of English Archive — Ivory Coast
notes: Single sample ('Ivory Coast 1', male, 24, Abidjan) of English in a native Ivorian accent with transcript; no Liberia or Cape Verde entries exist in IDEA.

name: IDEA International Dialects of English Archive — Sierra Leone
notes: Single sample ('Sierra Leone 1', male, 31, Freetown) with Comma Gets Cured passage plus free speech and an orthographic/phonetic transcript; tiny but transcribed accented-English reference.

name: IndabaxSenegal/asr-wolof-dataset
notes: 13,000 transcribed Wolof clips from the Senegal IndabaX community; many utterances contain French code-switching, which is realistic for Dakar speech.

name: Intron Health speech data platform (AfriVox-Transcribe, African Code-Switching Dataset)
notes: Commercial arm behind AfriSpeech/AfriSwitch; runs a paid contributor programme and enterprise licensing for African-accented and code-switched clinical speech. Hours not published.

name: IsiZulu Second Language Learner Speech Corpus
notes: 2,493 gold-standard recordings by L1 isiZulu teachers plus 9,639 L2-learner recordings annotated for phonemic and tonal errors (5.28 GB); unique for pronunciation scoring and tone modelling.

name: Janngu/pulaar-tts-dataset
notes: Very small (<1k samples, 49 kB manifest) Pulaar TTS seed set; viewer broken but licence is explicit CC-BY-4.0.

name: Joshua Project / Global Recordings Network language audio index (Umbundu example)
notes: RAW SOURCE: per-language pages indexing Global Recordings Network gospel-message and Bible audio, which is the ONLY audio in existence for most minority languages in this cluster (Kalanga, Nambya, Barwe, Nganguela, Chuwabo, Makonde etc.); short, scripted, unaligned and of mixed recording quality.

name: JW.org Amharic audio publications
notes: RAW SOURCE: professionally narrated Amharic audio with exactly matching published text (ideal forced-alignment material); only Amharic was confirmed in the language index for the Horn, so coverage of other Horn languages must be re-checked.

name: JW.org Krio audio library
notes: Full Krio-language site with audio dramas and Bible-reading dramas plus matching written text; multi-speaker dramatised audio, useful complement to single-narrator scripture reads. Copyright is restrictive.

name: JW.org Malagasy audio Bible and publications (Ny Soratra Masina, NWT 2021)
notes: Raw source verified via the public pub-media API: chapter-level MP3s for the whole Malagasy New World Translation plus magazines, with exactly matching online text - the single largest clean read-Malagasy audio+text pool.

name: Kalenjin speech (full)
notes: Consolidated Kalenjin speech set (mirrored at Kppwdfgu1/kalenjin-speech-full and cryptpesa/kalenjin-speech-full); appears to be a repackaging of the African Next Voices Kalenjin data.

name: KasuleTrevor/Afrivoice_ln_final
notes: Cleaned Lingala partition of Digital Umuganda's AfriVoice image-description speech data; card undocumented.

name: KasuleTrevor/Lingala_TTS
notes: 11.4k audio-transcript pairs (2-30s) curated for Lingala speech synthesis training.

name: Kencorpus collected data portal
notes: Project portal listing the raw audio/text collected per language and county; useful for locating un-packaged Kencorpus audio.

name: Kencorpus paper (arXiv)
notes: Describes collection protocol and the speech/QA/translation subsets; cite this to locate the speech-to-text portion of Kencorpus.

name: Kencorpus: Kenyan Language Corpus (Swahili, Dholuo, Luhya)
notes: Lacuna-funded Maseno University corpus: text plus ~1,500 speech/transcription items and a speech-to-text subset for three Kenyan languages; hours not stated in the record.

name: Kenyan Swahili ASR (cleaned)
notes: Cleaned Kenyan-Swahili ASR set; Kenyan Swahili differs markedly from Tanzanian standard Swahili so locale-specific sets matter.

name: Kenyan Voices
notes: Only 75 audio/text pairs, but genuinely Sheng-like: casual Kenyan English heavily code-switched with Swahili and local languages. Useful as a code-switch dev/test sample, far too small to train on.

name: Kikuyu ASR training dataset (Digital Green / Karya AIEP)
notes: 10k-100k paid-worker recordings of agricultural-extension sentences in Kikuyu, validated against transcripts; mirrored as CGIAR/KikuyuASR_trainingdataset. Permissive Apache licence.

name: Kikuyu audio (KevinKibe)
notes: Small Kikuyu audio/transcript dataset used for Whisper fine-tuning experiments.

name: Kikuyu transcription dataset
notes: Community-built Kikuyu audio/transcript pairs; the same author publishes an African-Kikuyu-TTS model trained on it.

name: Kinyarwanda TTS dataset (Digital Umuganda)
notes: 3,991 Kinyarwanda TTS prompt rows published by Digital Umuganda; the audio pairing/licence is under-documented on the card.

name: kittech_shona_dataset
notes: Tiny (108-clip) Zimbabwean set of religious/educational speech with Shona-English mixing in transcripts; one of the very few explicit Shona-English code-switch audio resources.

name: Klayt/baoule-common-voice
notes: 876 Common-Voice-style MP3 clips (319 train/267 val/290 test) from only 3 client IDs; the only openly downloadable Baoulé ASR set found, far too small to train on alone.

name: Kreol Morisien health-domain ASR corpus
notes: Purpose-built Kreol Morisien health-domain speech corpus described in the paper; no public download located - contact the authors. Confirms a Mauritian Creole ASR corpus exists but is not released.

name: Krio-Corpus (Jaward)
notes: Only public Krio corpus found on HuggingFace; modality (text vs audio), size and licence could not be verified - treat as a lead. No dedicated Krio SPEECH corpus was found anywhere; Krio audio exists only inside GRN/Bible religious recordings.

name: KrioVoice/Krio
notes: Placeholder repo of a Krio voice-data initiative — currently EMPTY (2.49 kB, no data files); listed only so the effort can be tracked.

name: Lacuna Fund language datasets index
notes: Index of Lacuna-funded language datasets; the single best directory for East African speech grants (Kencorpus, MakerereNLP, Swahili/Luganda TTS and others).

name: Lacuna Fund language/speech dataset portfolio
notes: Enabled 75+ ML datasets, 44 published, across agriculture, climate, health and low-resource language; the language portfolio is the funding source behind many entries in this catalogue (e.g. Kallaama for Wolof/Pulaar/Sereer, funded 2023). The site froze in July 2025 and leadership moved to the University of Pretoria DSFSI and AfriDSAI. I could not retrieve the per-dataset language listing in this pass (the datasets index pages returned empty to the fetcher) - a manual pass over lacunafund.org/projects/datasets is needed to enumerate the individual grants.
language_note: This source describes its coverage in prose rather than naming individual languages, so it carries no ISO 639-3 codes. The source's own wording is kept in `languages`.

name: laki35/somali-tts-dataset-11-speakers
notes: 1,200 clean multi-speaker clips (1.5-12s) tagged for phonetic balance; the only multi-speaker Somali TTS set found.

name: Lanfrica African AI Atlas (catalogue) and NaijaActions
notes: The main discovery index for African language resources (datasets, models, papers, policies) and the standard first stop when auditing coverage for a given language. Lanfrica also builds data directly - NaijaVoices, VoiceAfrica and NaijaActions are its own releases.
language_note: This source describes its coverage in prose rather than naming individual languages, so it carries no ISO 639-3 codes. The source's own wording is kept in `languages`.

name: Library of Congress - Algeria Berber-language audio recordings
notes: Digitised archival field/music recordings in Berber languages from Algeria; untranscribed and often musical, but one of the few archival audio pools that touches Chaoui.

name: Libyan Arabic smart voice agent corpus (Libyan Academy)
notes: Locally collected Libyan-dialect command/voice-agent recordings described in a Libyan Academy of Graduate Studies paper; no public distribution, listed because verified Libyan speech data is almost nonexistent.

name: Luganda ASR dataset (keystats)
notes: 256k audio/transcript rows (230k train / 25.6k validation) of Luganda MP3s; no dataset card, provenance and licence unverified.

name: Luganda/Swahili crowdsourced TTS data descriptor
notes: Peer-reviewed descriptor for the Mendeley Luganda/Swahili TTS corpus, documenting speaker-selection and curation criteria from Common Voice.

name: Lwazi English TTS Corpus
notes: Single-speaker TTS corpus with orthographic and phoneme-aligned transcriptions; Lwazi I produced comparable voices for all 11 languages.

name: Lwazi II Afrikaans TTS Corpus
notes: Phonemically aligned TTS corpus from Meraka/CSIR and NWU; part of a per-language Lwazi II TTS series on SADiLaR.

name: Lwazi II English TTS Corpus
notes: South African English single-speaker TTS corpus with phoneme-aligned transcriptions.

name: Lwazi II Sesotho TTS Corpus
notes: Sesotho TTS voice corpus; also the best available TTS starting point for Lesotho Sesotho.

name: M9and2M/Wolof_ASR_dataset
notes: 27.8 GB aggregation of ALFFA Wolof, Waxal-Wolof, FLEURS wo_sn and the Zenodo Wolof TTS data in pickle shards; the most convenient single Wolof training pool.

name: madoss/faso-speech-plus
notes: Extended version of faso-speech; exact added hours not documented on the dataset card.

name: Makerere AI Lab East African text & speech benchmark datasets (overview)
notes: Repository record for the Makerere AI Lab corpus programme (radio corpus, five-language Ugandan speech, keyword spotting); entry point for requesting unreleased splits.

name: MakerereNLP: Text & Speech for East Africa (Masakhane/Lacuna project)
notes: Lacuna-funded five-language Ugandan text+speech dataset project page; several splits are released piecemeal rather than as one archive.

name: makhuwa-trigrams-speech-text-parallel
notes: 154,253 parallel speech-text pairs for Emakhuwa - the ONLY Makhuwa audio resource found anywhere; provenance (human vs synthetic) undocumented, so audit before use.

name: MANIANGA/afrivoice-lin
notes: Community re-upload of AfriVoice Lingala; no dataset card, verify contents before use.

name: MANIANGA/afrivoice-sag
notes: Placeholder repo for Sango speech - currently EMPTY (2.5 kB). Recorded here as evidence that no open Sango speech corpus yet exists.

name: Masader (Arabic NLP & speech dataset catalogue)
notes: 500+ Arabic datasets annotated with 25+ attributes including dialect, modality and licence; the best single index for finding further country-level Arabic speech resources (also loadable as arbml/masader).

name: Masakhane speech and catalogue efforts
notes: Honest finding: Masakhane's ~45 HuggingFace datasets (MasakhaNER/NER2/POS, MAFAND-MT, MasakhaNEWS, AfriQA, AfriMMLU/AfriMGSM/AfriXNLI, AfroBench) are all TEXT - it publishes no speech corpus of its own. Its speech contribution is as a partner: Masakhane members co-authored BibleTTS and the AfricaNLP keyword-spotting work, and AfroBench (64 languages, 15 tasks, 22 datasets; arXiv 2311.07978) is the text counterpart to speech benchmarks like AfriVox.
language_note: This source describes its coverage in prose rather than naming individual languages, so it carries no ISO 639-3 codes. The source's own wording is kept in `languages`.

name: Masry: a Text-to-Speech System for Egyptian Arabic
notes: One of very few published Egyptian Arabic TTS efforts with a purpose-recorded single-speaker corpus; the dataset itself is not openly distributed - contact the authors.

name: Massively Multilingual Speech (MMS) / MMS-lab
notes: MMS built unlabelled + aligned religious (New Testament) audio for 1,100-4,000 languages, covering nearly every language in these four countries; the models are released but the underlying religious audio must be re-sourced from the original publishers.

name: Massively Multilingual Speech (MMS) — models and religious-reading pipeline
notes: MMS covers 1,107 languages for ASR/TTS and 4,000+ for LangID using New Testament readings; models and forced-aligner are public but the underlying audio is NOT redistributed — useful as a pipeline/alignment tool for Sahel Bible audio rather than as a dataset.

name: Mauritius Broadcasting Corporation (MBC) archive
notes: Raw source: national broadcaster carrying news and programmes in Kreol Morisien, French, English and Indic languages including Bhojpuri; no transcripts, so ASR data would need manual or pseudo-labelling.

name: Mayoiga/Soninke-dataset
notes: Only recent Soninke resource found on HuggingFace; modality (text vs audio) not documented on the card — verify before counting it as speech data. No confirmed Soninke speech corpus exists.

name: MDVC corpus (Moroccan Darija Voice Corpus)
notes: Purpose-built Moroccan Darija voice corpus described in a 2024 paper; distribution terms unclear - contact authors.

name: michsethowusu/english-seychelles-french-creole_sentence-pairs_mt560
notes: TEXT-ONLY (no audio): ~188k English-Seselwa sentence pairs extracted from MT560; listed because Seselwa has no speech corpus at all and this is the available text for TTS prompts/LM.

name: michsethowusu/vai-speech-text-parallel
notes: 23,300 Vai audio/text pairs (0.04-60 s clips) tagged for ASR, TTS and keyword spotting; provenance of the audio is not documented.

name: mixed_shona_dataset
notes: Companion 'mixed' Shona/English repo from the same Zimbabwean uploader; contents unverified, listed for completeness of code-switch leads.

name: ML-SUPERB / ML-SUPERB 2.0 (African subsets)
notes: 143-language multilingual LID+ASR benchmark (154k rows) assembled from Common Voice, FLEURS, ALFFA, NCHLT, VoxPopuli and others, with a 10-minute/1-hour few-shot design. The African subset is largely FLEURS + ALFFA + NCHLT re-packaged; ML-SUPERB 2.0 (Interspeech 2024, arXiv 2406.08641) adds fine-tuning/efficiency tracks and reports the largest performance gaps on African languages. Exact African language list per release not fully verified.

name: MMS (Massively Multilingual Speech) - MMS-lab religious-reading corpus
notes: Meta's 1,162-language ASR model; the model card's language list was read as including plt/mlg, mfe, crs, rcf, zdj, wni, swb and bho (worth re-verifying code by code). The underlying MMS-lab New-Testament read-speech audio is not redistributed, so the models and per-language adapters are the usable artefact.

name: MMS (Massively Multilingual Speech) TTS checkpoints
notes: Single-speaker VITS voices trained on religious (New Testament) readings; covers amh/orm/som/tir/sid/wal but NOT Afar, Tigre, Ge'ez, Saho, Kunama or Bilen. Example checkpoint: facebook/mms-tts-tir.

name: MMS TTS checkpoints — Côte d'Ivoire languages (facebook/mms-tts-*)
notes: Single-speaker VITS TTS checkpoints exist for these Ivorian languages (verified individually); training audio is NOT released. Notably there is NO MMS TTS for Baoulé (bci), Bété (bet/bev/btg) or Cebaara Sénoufo (sef).

name: MMS TTS checkpoints — Liberia languages (facebook/mms-tts-*)
notes: Verified MMS VITS checkpoints for five Liberian languages; no MMS TTS exists for Kpelle (xpe/gkp), Vai or Grebo (grj/gbo/gec). Training data unreleased.

name: MMS TTS checkpoints — Sierra Leone languages (facebook/mms-tts-*)
notes: Sierra Leone is the best-covered country in MMS TTS — checkpoints verified for all seven major languages; non-commercial licence and no released training audio.

name: MMS-ulab v2 (espnet/mms_ulab_v2)
notes: The MMS unlabelled-audio pool (religious readings) re-packaged by ESPnet; UNTRANSCRIBED so it is pre-training/SSL data only, but it is the single resource that covers essentially every language in my four countries.

name: Mooré Natural Emotions Speech Dataset
notes: 6,017 audio files in seven emotion classes harvested from Burkina Faso public radio; released on Kaggle (link given at end of the Springer chapter) — re-usable as Mooré acoustic data.

name: MosesJoshuaCoker/Krio_data_tts_v2
notes: 7.94 GB gated Krio TTS corpus in audiofolder format, <1K rows listed (row count likely per-file groupings); no documentation.

name: MosesJoshuaCoker/krio_dataset_novax
notes: Companion Krio dataset from the same uploader found in a HuggingFace search; contents and modality unverified.

name: Mozilla Common Voice (accent-tagged English, French, Portuguese, Arabic, Afrikaans, Swahili)
notes: Each clip carries self-reported accent/variant metadata, so African-accented subsets of English (Nigerian, Kenyan, South African, Ghanaian), French (Senegalese, Ivorian, Cameroonian, Maghrebi) and Portuguese (Angolan, Mozambican) can be filtered out. CC0 makes it the only commercially clean accented source at scale, but African accent volumes are small and self-reported. Note: from October 2025 distribution moved to Mozilla Data Collective.

name: Mozilla Common Voice (Basaa, bas)
notes: Basaa is a released Common Voice locale (public-domain CC0); validated hours are small but it is the only CC0 speech data for any Cameroonian language.

name: Mozilla Common Voice - Kalenjin (as repackaged for ASR)
notes: Kalenjin Common Voice audio converted to 16 kHz WAV with train/test/validated splits (5.6 GB); confirms Common Voice now has a Kalenjin locale.

name: Mozilla Common Voice - Luganda
notes: Luganda has been a substantial Common Voice language since CV5 (Makerere-led drive) and is notable for near gender-balanced contributions; exact hour count not confirmed here.

name: Mozilla Common Voice Emakhuwa localization
notes: Emakhuwa translation of the Common Voice web interface by Felermino Ali - evidence that an Emakhuwa Common Voice collection is being bootstrapped; no audio yet.

name: Multi-Language Conversational Telephone Speech 2011 - Arabic Group (LDC2019S02)
notes: Telephone conversations collected for language/dialect recognition evaluations; Arabic group spans several regional varieties, usable for telephone-channel ASR and dialect ID.

name: Multilingual ASR for Kinyarwanda, Swahili and Luganda (AfricaNLP 2023)
notes: Documents the exact Common Voice / FLEURS / ALFFA / Makerere data mixes and NeMo recipes for the three biggest East African ASR languages; good provenance reference rather than new data.

name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS) - SLR94
notes: Negative result recorded for completeness: MLS covers only English, German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese and Polish. No African languages, and no African varieties of the Romance languages it does cover.

name: multilingual-nchlt-dataset
notes: All eleven NCHLT languages in one package (DSFSI); the isiNdebele portion is South Ndebele (nbl), NOT Zimbabwean Northern Ndebele (nde) - a common and important confusion.

name: NaijaSynCor / Naija (Nigerian Pidgin) Spoken Corpus
notes: ANR NaijaSynCor project recorded a large sociolinguistic survey of spoken Naija across Nigeria; the public release is the syntactically annotated transcript treebank (UD_Naija-NSC, ~9k sentences), with the aligned audio held by the project. Best route to real spontaneous Pidgin speech is contacting the project.

name: Namibian Broadcasting Corporation (NBC) language radio services
notes: RAW SOURCE: NBC operates language radio services covering Oshiwambo, Otjiherero, Damara/Nama, Rukwangali, Silozi, Setswana, San, German, Afrikaans and English, with streams and podcasts on nbcplus.na - effectively the only substantial audio pool for most Namibian languages.

name: NCHLT isiZulu Auxiliary Speech Corpus
notes: Per-language auxiliary NCHLT release (XML + audio); part of the Aux1/Aux2 collection.

name: NCHLT Siswati Auxiliary Speech Corpus
notes: ~19.3 GB of orthographically transcribed siSwati broadband speech; the largest siSwati speech resource in existence and directly relevant to Eswatini.

name: NCHLT Speech Corpus - South African English
notes: Wide-band read speech from ~200 speakers per language for all 11 official languages, including South African English and Afrikaans; distributed via the NWU RMA (and an anonymous FTP mirror). The backbone SA English/Afrikaans ASR resource.

name: NCHLT Speech Corpus - Tshivenda
notes: ~49,700 read utterances from 200 speakers with age/gender and pronunciation-quality annotation; South African Tshivenda but directly transferable to Venda speakers in southern Zimbabwe, for whom no local corpus exists.

name: NCHLT Speech Corpus - Xitsonga
notes: ~47,800 read utterances from 190 speakers; the only substantial Tsonga speech corpus and the practical proxy for Zimbabwean Shangani and Mozambican Changana/Xitsonga.

name: NCHLT Speech II Corpus
notes: Second NCHLT English collection released in 2016; hours not stated on the record page.

name: NCHLT Xitsonga Auxiliary Speech Corpus
notes: Per-language auxiliary NCHLT Xitsonga release.

name: NCHLT-inlang Pronunciation Dictionaries
notes: Not audio: the companion grapheme-to-phoneme pronunciation dictionaries and phone sets for all 11 languages, required to build ASR/TTS on NCHLT and Lwazi audio.

name: Ndebele Bible (Northern Ndebele text)
notes: TEXT ONLY: full Northern Ndebele (isiNdebele, Zimbabwe) Bible. Listed because it is the obvious script for a Ndebele TTS/aligned-audio effort - no Northern Ndebele speech corpus exists at all.

name: Nexdata off-the-shelf speech datasets
notes: 245 off-the-shelf speech datasets, of which the public catalogue exposes Arabic (e.g. a 268 h Arabic full-duplex set) and a 59-item 'Others' bucket. No sub-Saharan African language is advertised on the public listing; African coverage would have to be commissioned. Treat advertised African capability as unverified.

name: ngia/ASR_pulaar
notes: Community Pulaar ASR set on HuggingFace; card metadata sparse, size unverified (a processed variant exists as TaphaFall/ASR_pulaar_processed).

name: nicolingua project repo (data + West African wav2vec model)
notes: Download scripts, AWS mirrors and the pretrained West African wav2vec checkpoint for both nicolingua corpora.

name: nicolingua-0004 West African Virtual Assistant ASR corpus (OpenSLR SLR106)
notes: 10,083 labelled virtual-assistant command utterances from 49 speakers (16F/33M, ages 5-76) across many devices; the only transcribed Susu/Maninka/Pular speech data in existence.

name: Nigerian Accented English Dataset
notes: 3,400 audio/text pairs of Nigerian-accented English from multiple contributors; permissive licence makes it usable commercially, unlike AfriSpeech.

name: Nigerian Pidgin ASR Corpus v1.0
notes: 4,280 utterances (2,710/677/892 train/dev/test) of read Nigerian Pidgin covering sport, politics, health; the main openly licensed Naija speech set (arXiv:2010.11123 lineage).

name: Nigerian Pidgin TTS dataset
notes: Community Naija TTS corpus; size/licence not verified. Related pidgin speech uploads include Rexe/nigerian-pidgin-speech, grazef6/nigerian_pidgin_asr_v2, timniel/Pidgin_ASR_Dataset_Combined and WAZOBIALABS/nigerian-pidgin-voice-text.

name: Ny Baiboly (nybaiboly.net) Malagasy Bible audio and radio archive
notes: Raw source: Malagasy Bible reading audio plus radio programmes alongside the full text; already used for 2.2h of VoxMg, and the site also carries a Shimaore (Mayotte) section.

name: Nyana-Eval (Bambara ASR benchmark)
notes: Curated human-evaluation benchmark drawn from Kunkado test data, jeli street interviews and GAIFE readings; small but the reference eval set for Bambara.

name: nyanjaspeech (HF)
notes: Community-uploaded Nyanja speech repo appearing alongside a BembaSpeech mirror by the same user; contents and licence unverified.

name: OlameMend/Ewondo-TTS
notes: 7,970 aligned audio-transcript rows of Ewondo (largely scripture/religious text); the only dedicated Ewondo speech corpus found.

name: Omnilingual ASR Corpus
languages: multiple (348 under-served languages incl. Malian and Burkinabè languages)
notes: Meta FAIR commissioned spontaneous speech + transcripts for 348 under-served languages (547k rows); North African entries include Egyptian Arabic, Algerian Saharan Arabic and Tarifit (rif_Tfng) - one of the very few transcribed Tarifit sources anywhere.

name: Open.Bible (Biblica) Creative-Commons scripture text and audio
languages: Multiple African languages (Nigeria, Ghana, Uganda and others)
notes: Biblica's CC-licensed release hub for Bible text and audio; the upstream source of BibleTTS. African entries seen include Acholi (Uganda), Adele (Ghana), Abureni, Ajiya, Alago and Kurama (Nigeria). Audio availability is per-translation and must be checked title by title; licence is unusually permissive for scripture audio, which is why it is the backbone of African TTS work.
language_note: This source describes its coverage in prose rather than naming individual languages, so it carries no ISO 639-3 codes. The source's own wording is kept in `languages`.

name: OpenBible Swahili (verse-aligned)
notes: 31,103 verse-level segments (29,233 after cleaning) of the Biblica Neno Swahili audio Bible, MMS/CTC force-aligned; the most usable single-speaker Swahili TTS corpus.

name: ORTC (Office de Radio et Television des Comores) archive
notes: Raw source: national broadcaster with Comorian-language radio ('La matinale', 'Nyaswiya', 'Ulozi') and TV ('Dakika 26', 'Msafara'), regional stations on Anjouan and Moheli, live stream and YouTube/Facebook back-catalogue; untranscribed.

name: oza75/bambara-asr
notes: 38 GB gated Bambara ASR collection (contact info required); no card documentation, but among the biggest single Bambara audio dumps.

name: oza75/bambara-tts
notes: 39.1 GB of Bambara audio with Bambara text, French translations, pyannote speaker embeddings and HDBSCAN speaker clusters; sourced from Mali Pense and DeepFilterNet-denoised.

name: Pangloss Collection - Bougiote (Bejaia Kabyle) corpus
notes: Time-aligned narratives in the urban Bejaia (Bougie) variety of Kabyle; small documentation corpus, open access.

name: Pangloss Collection - Senhaja de Srair (Zerqet) corpus
notes: Documentation recordings of the endangered Senhaja de Srair Berber variety of the Moroccan Rif, time-aligned with transcription and translation; essentially the only audio corpus for this variety.

name: Pangloss Collection - Siwi corpus
notes: Open-access time-aligned Siwi recordings with transcription and translation; small but directly usable for forced-alignment / low-resource ASR experiments.

name: Pangloss Collection - Tasahlite (Kabyle) corpus
notes: Open-access time-aligned recordings of the Tasahlite variety of Kabyle with transcription and French translation; valuable for dialect variation within Kabyle beyond Common Voice's standardised reading.

name: papasega/Waxal_Multiling_4_SER-Wolof (speech emotion recognition)
notes: 3,770 labelled Wolof audio clips built for emotion recognition; re-usable as extra Wolof acoustic data for ASR/TTS pretraining.

name: Parliament of South Africa - plenary video/audio and Hansard
notes: RAW SOURCE: Parliament TV/Radio streams and podcasts plus official Hansard transcripts of the same sittings - a genuinely multilingual, naturally code-switched aligned-audio-and-text resource awaiting alignment.

name: Paywinful/akan_asr_dataset
notes: 16,900 Akan clips (15-30 s) with speaker age/gender, device, environment and locale ak_gh metadata — the field set matches UGSpeechData, so likely a derived redistribution.

name: perrynelson/waxal-wolof
notes: 2,380 transcribed utterances (4.8-114 s) from the Waxal WhatsApp collection; test split larger than train, so use with care.

name: Pidgin ASR Dataset Combined
notes: Community aggregation of several Nigerian Pidgin ASR sources into one loadable dataset; provenance and licence need checking before reuse.

name: Portuguese-Speech-Dataset (Speech-data)
notes: Same publisher as the 94h Chichewa set; variety unspecified, worth checking whether any African Portuguese speakers are included since the publisher does source in Southern Africa.

name: portuguese-speech-recognition-dataset (UniDataPro)
notes: VENDOR sample on HF; variety is unspecified and almost certainly European/Brazilian, so it is a fallback rather than African Portuguese - no Mozambican or Angolan Portuguese speech corpus was found anywhere.

name: prajdabre/KreolMorisienMT
notes: TEXT-ONLY (no audio): ~85k Kreol Morisien MT/bitext pairs, the main Mauritian Creole NLP resource; matters here only as transcript/LM material for a future Kreol ASR or TTS system.

name: princekouame1/nouchi-lexicon
notes: TEXT-ONLY Nouchi lexicon — the only Nouchi language resource of any kind found; there is no Nouchi speech data, so this is listed as pronunciation-lexicon/LM support for future ASR.

name: Qfrency South African TTS Voices
notes: Commercial South African TTS voices derived from the CSIR/NWU Lwazi voice-building work; voices are sold rather than the underlying corpora.

name: Quran Speech-to-Text data - SLR132
notes: Multi-reciter Quran audio aligned to verse text (up to 6,236 ayah across 114 surah) with a TSV ready for ML. Classical Arabic, highly stylised recitation - relevant to North African Arabic pipelines mainly as pronunciation/alignment data.

name: Radio Ergo Somali podcast/broadcast archive
notes: RAW SOURCE: daily Somali humanitarian radio bulletins archived as dated SoundCloud podcast episodes plus matching written articles - the most transcript-adjacent Somali audio archive available.

name: Radiodiffusion Television de Djibouti (RTD) archive
notes: RAW SOURCE and the only Djibouti-specific option found: national radio/TV with 'RTD en Direct' live streaming plus active YouTube and Facebook channels. This is the only realistic route to Djiboutian French and Djibouti Afar/Somali speech.

name: rbaks/malagasy-asr-normalized-v2
notes: Gated (contact-sharing) Malagasy ASR corpus, 20.5 GB parquet in the 10K-100K sample band with normalised transcripts; empty card, no licence stated.

name: Reunion Creole speech dataset
notes: ~2,810 audio rows with paired French and Reunion Creole transcriptions plus WER/BLEU model outputs; one of the only Reunion Creole speech resources anywhere. Licence unstated.

name: RFI Afrique audio archive
notes: Decades of daily French-language African broadcast journalism (plus RFI's Hausa, Swahili, Mandenkan and Fulfulde services) with podcast feeds and often matching article text - the best raw pool for African-accented French. Rights are reserved; scraping needed.

name: rifailabs Comorian language text resources (dictionaries, lessons, proverbs, Swadesh)
notes: TEXT-ONLY companions to the Comorian speech sets: shingazidja_dictionary, shimwali_dictionary, shimaore_dictionary, shimaore_lessons, shindzuani_lessons, shikomori_phrases/proverbs, comorian_swadesh - the pronunciation/text backbone for Comorian ASR/TTS.

name: rifailabs/shikomori-stt-multi
notes: The only dedicated Comorian ASR corpus found: ~2.95k audio+text rows, 1.27 GB, gated behind contact sharing; paired with rifailabs' shikomori-stt-multi, whisper-shikomori-latin/arabic and mms-1b-zdj models.

name: rifailabs/shikomori-tts-synthetic
notes: ~72.5k synthetic Comorian TTS pairs (6.97 GB), gated; synthetic so quality is bounded by the generating voice, but it is the only Comorian TTS-scale resource and backs rifailabs/shikomori-tts and km-tts-v2.

name: RobotsMali/bam-asr-early
notes: ~41.1k rows combining jeli-asr, the oza75 Mali-Pense readings and RobotsMali field collection; the standard early Bambara ASR mix.

name: RTC Cape Verde on-demand archive (Rádiotelevisão Caboverdiana)
notes: Dated archives of TCV television news (Jornal da Noite) and RCV radio bulletins (Jornal da Tarde, Primeiro Jornal); interface and most news is Cape Verdean Portuguese, with Kabuverdianu in interviews/vox-pops. No transcripts.

name: RTI / RTIPlay archive (Radiodiffusion Télévision Ivoirienne)
notes: State broadcaster with on-demand replay (RTIPlay.ci) of RTI 1/RTI 2/La 3 news bulletins and reports plus Fréquence 2 and Radio CI radio archives; all in Ivorian French, no transcripts.

name: Rádio Moçambique online archive
notes: RAW SOURCE: national public broadcaster news portal with online radio channels, programme archives and YouTube; the only realistic large-scale route to Mozambican Portuguese and Mozambican Bantu-language audio, no transcripts.

name: SABC radio and television archives
notes: RAW SOURCE: SABC runs a full-language-service radio network (Ukhozi FM, Umhlobo Wenene, RSG, Lesedi, Motsweding, Thobela, Ligwalagwala, Phalaphala, Munghana Lonene, Ikwekwezi) - the largest untapped broadcast audio pool for all 11 languages; no open archive, licensing/scraping required.

name: SADiLaR Language Resource Management Agency repository
notes: Canonical distribution point for NCHLT and Lwazi speech/text corpora; the nearest thing to a regional repository for cross-border Zimbabwe/Mozambique languages (Tshivenda, Xitsonga).

name: SALT speech datasets documentation / code
notes: Loader/tooling and docs (https://salt.sunbird.ai/tutorials/07-speech-datasets/) describing the multispeaker and studio speech configs; needed to actually assemble the SALT speech splits.

name: Sample Dagbani-TTS-Dataset
notes: Sample Dagbani single-speaker TTS set in the same Institute of African Digital Humanities series; licence forbids generative use.

name: SautiDB-Naija
notes: 900+ L2 English recordings labelled by L1 (Yoruba, Igbo, Edo, Efik-Ibibio, Igala); used for Nigerian accent-embedding experiments — one of the very few resources touching Edo, Efik/Ibibio and Igala at all.

name: SBC Seychelles (Seychelles Broadcasting Corporation) archive
notes: Raw source: national broadcaster publishing news in Kreol Seselwa, English and French with an SBC+ streaming service; written Creole news items on the same site give partial pseudo-parallel text.

name: scales_shona_ai
notes: Dataset from a Zimbabwean company (Scales ZW) building Shona AI; size, licence and modality unverified.

name: serge-wilson/wolof_speech_transcription
notes: 14,800 Wolof audio/transcript pairs (2.3-12.5 s) with train/test splits; licence not declared on the card.

name: Sesotho multi-speaker TTS corpus
notes: Low-cost multi-voice Sesotho TTS corpus (MuST, NWU).

name: Setswana multi-speaker TTS corpus
notes: Low-cost multi-voice Setswana TTS corpus (MuST, NWU); also the best open TTS resource for Botswana Setswana.

name: Shaip Swahili speech data catalogue
notes: Commercial off-the-shelf and bespoke Swahili collections (call centre, virtual assistant, scripted/spontaneous ASR); representative of the vendor tier (Appen, Defined.ai, Nexdata, Way With Words also sell Swahili).

name: shona-speech (badrex)
notes: 17,600 transcribed Shona clips from 28 speakers with train/dev/test splits; appears to be an AfriVoice-derived repackaging, licence not stated.

name: shona-speech-dataset (Shunya Labs)
notes: Vendor-published Shona ASR set (3,780 clips, 3.5-53s) from Shunya Labs; small but independently collected, licence unstated so confirm before commercial use.

name: shona_asr (realtime-speech)
notes: Demonstration repo containing a single Shona audio/transcript pair; effectively unusable for training, listed only so it is not mistaken for a corpus.

name: shunyalabs/kabuverdianu-speech-dataset
notes: 3,950 audio/transcript rows (2,720/366/864 split), clips 3.5-40 s; the only dedicated Kabuverdianu ASR corpus found, variant (Sotavento vs Barlavento) not declared.

name: shunyalabs/lingala-speech-dataset
notes: 4,420 audio-text pairs with train/val/test splits; encyclopaedic prompt text suggests read or synthesised-prompt speech.

name: SIB-FLEURS (WueNLP)
notes: Topic-labelled FLEURS derivative (102 languages) usable for spoken topic classification as well as ASR; Amharic 955, Somali 993, Oromo 597 rows.

name: skydheere/soomali-asr-dataset
notes: 21.5k audio/transcript pairs with train/val/test splits (17.2k/2.15k/2.15k); mixes single words and full sentences.

name: SLBC (Sierra Leone Broadcasting Corporation)
notes: National radio and TV broadcaster; broadcasts include English plus local-language bulletins, making it the main potential source of spontaneous Krio/Mende/Temne broadcast speech. Online archive availability unverified.

name: Somali speech / Somali ASR (community sets)
notes: Community Somali audio corpus; related sets include nurfarah57/somali_asr and FarmerlineML/somali_cleaned_dataset. Useful for Somali in Kenya, dialect/locale unverified.

name: Somali TTS datasets
notes: 5,000 Somali text/audio pairs for speech synthesis; Somalia-centric rather than Kenyan-Somali, but transferable to Kenya's Somali-speaking north-east.

name: South African Directory Enquiries (SADE) Name Corpus
notes: Audio + tagged orthographic transcriptions of South African personal/place names read by L1 speakers of four languages (494 MB); built for directory-enquiry ASR and cross-lingual name pronunciation.

name: South African English parliamentary speech resources
notes: Method and resource built by aligning SA Parliament audio with Hansard to produce South African English acoustic training data; the underlying Parliament of South Africa audio/Hansard archive remains a large scrapeable raw source for SA English.

name: soynade-research/Bambara-Speech-Translation-Data
notes: Bambara audio with French translations for speech-to-text translation; overlaps with jeli-asr lineage.

name: Speech Accent Archive (GMU)
notes: Every speaker reads the same English elicitation paragraph; includes many African L1 backgrounds (Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa, Amharic, Swahili, Afrikaans, Arabic etc.). Tiny per-speaker duration, so best for accent ID rather than ASR training. Kaggle mirror at kaggle.com/datasets/rtatman/speech-accent-archive.

name: Spoken data corpus for Coloured Afrikaans, Setswana and Sesotho sa Leboa (SADiLaR project)
notes: 300+ 'Northwind and the Sun' readings with TextGrid acoustic annotation; built for phonetic/sociolinguistic study of Coloured Afrikaans but reusable as forced-aligned read speech.

name: STEM content Swahili speech
notes: Swahili speech recorded for STEM/education content generation; domain-specific vocabulary (maths, science) absent from general corpora.

name: STT-Kinyarwanda (Coqui STT recipe + data prep)
notes: Digital Umuganda Coqui-STT Kinyarwanda training repo; documents the exact CV subsets and LM data used.

name: Studio Kalangou (Fondation Hirondelle Niger) broadcast archive
notes: RAW SOURCE: daily news bulletins in five languages published as downloadable MP3s since 2016, with French-language written summaries — the single richest harvestable archive for Nigerien languages.

name: Studio Sifaka Malagasy radio podcast archive
notes: Raw source: UN-backed youth radio producing two hours daily of Malagasy news, magazines and debates, archived as SoundCloud podcasts - the best spontaneous/broadcast Malagasy audio, but untranscribed.

name: Studio Tamani (Fondation Hirondelle Mali) broadcast archive
notes: RAW SOURCE: daily journals in French, Bambara, Sonrhaï (Songhay), Peulh (Maasina Fulfulde) and Tamasheq, each posted as a direct MP3 with dated URLs; the only practical audio source for Malian Songhay and Maasina Fulfulde.

name: sudoping01/open-bambara-asr-dataset
notes: 16.1 GB gated Bambara ASR aggregation from the MALIBA-AI community (behind the maliba-asr models).

name: Sukuma Speech Corpus
notes: 21.7k utterances (17.7k/1.6k/2.4k splits) recorded around Mwanza with speaker gender, age, education, occupation, environment and SNR metadata; the best-documented Tanzanian minority-language corpus.

name: Sukuma-Voices
notes: ~8,000 transcribed Sukuma clips (1.4-30 s), largely scripture-derived narration, from Tanzanian AI company Sartify; an ACL variant is also published.

name: sulaimank/lingala-AMMI
notes: Lingala speech split associated with AMMI/African Masters ASR experiments; dataset card is empty so hours unverified.

name: sulaimank/lingala_LRSC
notes: Another HF mirror of the Lingala Read Speech Corpus used in Makerere/ASR-Africa fine-tuning work; metadata undocumented.

name: Sunbird AI SALT (Sunbird African Language Technology)
notes: 25,000 parallel sentences on locally relevant topics (agriculture, health, society) across 10 languages, of which ~5,000 have multi-speaker and studio speech recordings - so it supports ASR, TTS, MT and speech translation. Overlaps the East Africa cluster; listed here because it is the anchor multilingual Ugandan resource. Sunbird also publishes urban-noise-uganda-61k (61k labelled urban sound clips from Kampala/Entebbe, the first large African urban-sound dataset).

name: surafelabebe/amharic_clear_audio_tts
notes: Community-curated clean Amharic TTS audio; one of several small HF Amharic TTS sets (see also Namuorg/amharic-tts-*, Hope226/amharic_tts).

name: Svngoku/kikongo-bible-asr
notes: 4,868 Bible-derived Kikongo items aligned for ASR/TTS; documentation is a template so provenance of the audio needs checking.

name: Svngoku/lingala-asr-dataset
notes: Community-built Lingala ASR set from the Congolese NLP developer Svngoku; small and undocumented.

name: Svngoku/speech-recognition-congolese-languages
notes: 1,270 labelled clips (0.06-20s) for spoken language identification across three Congolese languages; reusable as ASR seed data.

name: Swahili speech data (Professor)
notes: 100k-1M sample Swahili ASR/TTS collection; part of a family of same-author sets covering Dholuo, Kalenjin, Maasai, Acholi and Lusoga (e.g. .../dholuo-speech-data), all thinly documented.

name: Swahili words speech-text parallel corpus
notes: 411k very short (0.3-5 s) Swahili word/phrase clips with transcripts; suited to keyword spotting, lexicon and pronunciation work rather than sentence ASR.

name: Swahili-English Code-Switching ASR (liva-ai)
notes: Human-verified multi-speaker Swahili-English code-switching conversations; the public sample is only 15 rows (vendor teaser for a larger commercial collection).

name: Synthetic Acholi VITS 22.5k (TTS-generated speech)
notes: Synthetic VITS/MMS-generated Acholi audio used for ASR data augmentation; matching sets exist for Ateso and Runyankole - synthetic, not human speech.

name: Synthetic Text Corpus for African Language ASR
notes: Text-only corpus intended as prompt material / language-model data for African ASR pipelines; no audio, listed here because it is the companion resource for several of the TTS sets above.

name: Tamazight-ASR-Dataset-v2
notes: 20.3k segments (18.3k train / 2.04k test, 0.37-13.5 s) cut from video sources with Tamazight and Arabic transcriptions; Apache-2.0 and one of the few commercially usable Tamazight ASR sets.

name: Tamazight-Speech-to-Arabic-Text
notes: 20.3k Tamazight audio segments paired with ARABIC-script text (speech translation rather than same-language transcription); from the Tamazight-NLP community, which also ships Coqui TTS spaces and NLLB models for Tamazight.

name: TARC (Tunisian Arabish Corpus)
notes: Text-only (not audio) corpus of Tunisian written in Latin 'Arabish'/Arabizi with Arabic-script and morphological layers; listed because it is the key resource for building Arabizi language models and transcription conventions for Tunisian ASR output.

name: The Edinburgh International Accents of English Corpus (EdAcc)
notes: Free dyadic video-call conversations across many self-reported English varieties including several African ones; each speaker has a documented linguistic profile. African share is small but it is the best conversational accent benchmark.

name: tunis-ai/arabic_speech_corpus
notes: Tunisian-hosted mirror of the single-speaker MSA 'Arabic Speech Corpus' used as a TTS/phonetiser base for Tunisian systems; the source voice is Levantine-MSA, so not a Tunisian-dialect voice.

name: Turkana speech dataset
notes: 3,320 Turkana WAV/transcript pairs - the only Turkana speech data located; a turkana-2.0-dataset follow-up exists from the same group. Non-commercial licence.

name: TutlaytAI/tamazight_asr
notes: 51.1k audio-text pairs (35.8k train / 15.3k test, 0.7-12.7 s) combining Kabyle and Standard Moroccan Tamazight; mixed CC-BY-4.0 / CC-BY-NC-4.0 components, so check per-row provenance.

name: TWB Voice TTS Hausa 1.0 (sample set)
notes: Hausa counterpart of the CLEAR Global TTS sample sets; full corpus available on request.

name: TWB Voice TTS Kanuri 1.0 (sample set)
notes: 10% public sample of a single-female-speaker 48 kHz Central Kanuri TTS corpus; full set on request from CLEAR Global. A matching Hausa TTS corpus exists (CLEAR-Global/TWB-Voice-Hausa-TTS-1.0).

name: Uganda Court Speech
notes: 23.4k transcribed clips (1-20 s) from Ugandan court proceedings; legal-domain Ugandan-English ASR data, licence unstated.

name: Ugandan English (ajikadev)
notes: Ugandan-English speech collection by the same author as the court-speech set; metadata sparse, needs inspection before use.

name: UGSpeechData Akan slice (Farmerline/UG HCI 2025 release)
notes: HuggingFace-packaged Akan subset of UGSpeechData prepared jointly by Farmerline and the UG HCI Lab; convenient ASR-ready format.

name: unza-nyanja
notes: Small University of Zambia Nyanja ASR repo (1.8MB, metadata/transcripts rather than bulk audio); undocumented, check Files before relying on it.

name: Urban Noise Uganda 61k
notes: 61k geo-tagged 16 kHz urban soundscape clips from Kampala/Entebbe (Scientific Data descriptor); not speech, but the right noise source for augmenting Ugandan ASR.

name: Vambo AI (Shona ASR/TTS platform)
notes: Zimbabwean startup offering Shona-first ASR, TTS and voice cloning APIs for 60+ African languages; underlying training data is not published but they are a likely data-partnership route.

name: VOA Africa services audio archive
notes: VOA's African-language and African-English services publish daily audio with parallel written stories; much VOA output is US-government public domain, which makes it unusually attractive for building accented-English and African-French corpora.

name: VOA Horn of Africa language services (Amharic, Afaan Oromoo, Tigrinya, Somali)
notes: RAW SOURCE and the single biggest harvestable pool for the Horn: decades of daily radio/TV programmes with parallel web articles across four services (amharic.voanews.com, voaafaanoromoo.com, tigrigna.voanews.com, voasomali.com). US-government work, so copyright is relatively permissive; some domains block automated fetching.

name: VOA Studio 7 Zimbabwe
notes: RAW SOURCE: daily radio/video programming in Shona, Ndebele and English with accompanying web articles; US-government-produced content is often public domain, making this the best harvestable Ndebele broadcast source.

name: Vocal data in the Dioula language related to the numbers 1-4 (Zenodo)
notes: 296 MB of Dioula number pronunciations across varied speakers, accents and acoustic conditions; the original release behind faso-speech-dioula-digits.

name: voice_datasets (open-source speech/audio dataset index)
notes: Curated index of 95+ open speech/sound datasets; used here to cross-check Arabic and African entries. Meta-resource, not a dataset.
language_note: This source describes its coverage in prose rather than naming individual languages, so it carries no ISO 639-3 codes. The source's own wording is kept in `languages`.

name: VoxCommunis
notes: Forced-aligned phone-level annotations and acoustic models derived from Common Voice, including Amharic; useful for phonetic work and TTS aligners.

name: VoxPopuli
notes: Negative result recorded for completeness: VoxPopuli is European Parliament speech only - 18 transcribed European languages and 15 L2-English accents all from European L1s. No African language and no African-accented English. Do not budget for it in an African strategy.

name: Way With Words African speech data catalogue (defunct)
notes: Formerly a major seller of South African / African accented speech datasets (incl. a 50h conversational SA English set). Way With Words SA (Pty) Ltd ceased operations 31 August 2026 and no longer licenses data; the UK entity waywithwords.net continues services only. Logged so the dead link is not re-chased.

name: Way With Words Speech Data (African language collections)
notes: Durban-based vendor that collected and licensed African-language speech data and was a delivery partner on African Next Voices; note Way With Words SA ceased normal operations on 31 August 2026 and no longer accepts dataset-licensing enquiries (UK entity waywithwords.net continues).

name: WOLOF TTS (Text To Speech) Data — Diop et al.
notes: Two professional Wolof actors (1M/1F), each reading 20,000+ sentences from news/Wikipedia with expert-checked phoneme coverage; 1.3 GB, the main open Wolof TTS resource.

name: Yaounde French Speech Corpus (CTELL, West Point)
notes: Original technical report and data for the Yaounde component later folded into OpenSLR 57; recorded for pedagogical ASR research, approved for public release.

name: YODAS2-Sidon (sarulab-speech/yodas2_sidon)
notes: YouTube-derived (YODAS-2) speech with Sidon audio restoration, 149+ languages at 24 kHz FLAC; includes an Afar subset, which is otherwise almost unobtainable. Transcripts are YouTube captions, so quality varies.

name: YodiV3 / Eyaa-Tom (AfricaNLP 2025 paper)
notes: Paper documenting Eyaa-Tom composition (min. 2,000 parallel religious sentences per language) and the Lom evaluation metric; Umbaji also released MMS-TTS fine-tunes for Gen and Aja.

name: Yogera crowdsourced speech - Acholi
notes: ~6.8 GB of Acholi audio from the Yogera crowdsourcing platform (Uganda Open Source AI Lab); no dataset card, contact-sharing gate.

name: Yogera crowdsourced speech - Luganda
notes: Luganda partition of the Yogera crowdsourced speech collection.

name: Yogera crowdsourced speech - Lusoga
notes: One of the very few Lusoga speech datasets; Yogera/Kukuza AI crowdsourced audio, undocumented.

name: Yogera crowdsourced speech - Runyankole
notes: Runyankole/Rukiga speech from the Yogera platform; complements the SALT studio Runyankole recordings.

name: Yoruba-TTS-Dataset (Institute of African Digital Humanities)
notes: 319 MB of Yoruba audio/transcript pairs in 17 folders; the Nwulite Obodo Open Data Licence explicitly forbids generative AI, voice cloning and commercial use, so it is close to unusable for TTS training despite the name.

name: Zambezi Voice Bemba text corpus
notes: Text-only companion release (prompts/transcripts) for Zambezi Voice; needed for ASR language models and TTS front-ends, siblings exist for nya, toi and loz.

name: Zimbabwe Parliament Hansard, Web TV and Web Radio
notes: RAW SOURCE: National Assembly and Senate Hansard PDFs alongside Web TV and Web Radio streams; a near-parallel speech/transcript pipeline for Zimbabwean English with Shona and Ndebele interventions.
